narrative:
On Thursday March 13th, 2025, the crew change bus had a road accident. It was 18h30 and after a heavy rain at the 
time of the incident.
The bus driver was driving too close to the road edge to avoid potholes of the road section. While doing so a part of 
the road edge collapsed under the right front bus tire making the bus end its trajectory on the pipelines on the side 
of the road with 28 pax on board.
Immediate action: 
• An alcohol test was performed (negative).
• The TAG removed. 
• Rearranged work because of restricted mobility due to ankle sprain.

At around 4am on 1st of May, the two men on the crane were assigned to a new location. The operation involved 
depositing the counterweights. Following a counter-order from the supervisor, they had to carry out a final lift 
before going on to the new location. The spider chains were replaced on the counterweights. As the chains are 
lifted, one of the hooks gets caught in the guide of the counterweight. When the chains come off, they have a spring 
effect. The banksman can't reasonably control three of them and the fourth spins around him with his back lower. 
The spider chain hit the banksman at the back. The IP received pain killer treatment before transferring to hospital 
by chopper. The IP suffered a permanent impairment injury.

On 18 August 2025, a team was installing a 6-inch pipe over a 35-metre section between two lines. This pipe was 
also to be used during WO operations. During the operation, the team separated a 6-inch pipe from a 2-inch pipe, 
both of which had previously been tied together with cords. During the lifting phase, the cords were gradually cut 
to separate the two pipes. When the third cord was cut, the tension accumulated in the 6-inch pipe, which was 
bent at the time, was suddenly released. The pipe rebounded and struck an operator's right leg between the ankle 
and knee, causing an open fracture. The supervisor was immediately informed, the control room was alerted, and 
emergency procedures were quickly implemented.

On January 19, 2025, during restart attempts of the HP-A Gas Compressor following corrective maintenance, 
an unusually loud noise was heard from the exhaust. Seconds later, the fire alarm was triggered, and it was 
observed that the exhaust structure had fallen off. Technicians in the vicinity immediately pressed the compressor’s 
emergency stop button and evacuated the facility. Simultaneously, the emergency response team was activated, and 
the on-scene commander initiated a full facility shutdown using a manual call point near the compressor building. 
Once the source of the loud noise was confirmed to be the HP-A compressor, with the exhaust lying on the ground, 
the area was cordoned off, and an investigation was launched. The compressor was manually shut down, and the 
ESD-1 emergency stop was activated.

During a heavy rainstorm, two aluminium composite panels (component of the external cladding material for the 
Office building) dislodged and dropped. The two (2) panels, each weighing 9.8kgs and measuring 1.11x1.49ms, 
dropped from about a height of 22.35 meters. The fallen panels were found Infront of the South Wing Power room, 
and the affected area was promptly cordoned off to prevent further hazards. Additionally, multiple panels were 
observed hanging loosely, posing a potential safety risk to occupants and visitors.

At about 02:21hrs, while rig crew was picking 4” drill pipe, a single drill pipe was picked from Catwalk to the rig 
floor with Air winch tugger. The IP removed thread protector from the single pipe while another floorman attempted 
to guide the pipe into the mouse hole. The pipe missed the mouse hole, hit the rig floor and also hit the IP on his 
right ear and shoulder. IP was move to Clinic.

At about 10:30 hours, a company-owned light vehicle in a security convoy travelling veered off the road and collided 
with an electric pole. The driver and accompanying customer were safely evacuated and transported to the Clinic for 
appropriate medical evaluation / attention.

On 3rd June 2025, at about 2:15pm, during a test digging on a 6" test line right of way, the excavator bucket made 
contact with a buried 11KVA composite electrical cable. The incident resulted in a dent/superficial cut on the cable.
Release of propane from a temp. storage tank.

A 9 kg metal plate detached from the conveyor railway and fell approximately 6.5–10 m onto the deck below.
No personnel were struck; however, dropped-object energy indicated fatality potential.
The plate was originally installed as a dropped-object prevention measure. Over time it deteriorated and was 
displaced due to a misaligned and stretched conveyor belt, which pushed the plate out of position.
Operations on the starboard conveyor were stopped, the area below was barricaded, and a rope-access inspection 
of similar installations was initiated.

At approximately 06:30, lifting operations were being conducted to move spools from the main deck to the cellar/
sub-cellar deck.
Because no direct lifting path existed, the crew chose to lift the load through a slickline hatch, which constituted 
a complex lift and was not covered by the approved PTW. The crane operator had no line of sight and was 
communicating by radio only.
During lifting, the hook snagged the hatch plate. The rigger, who was standing on the hatch cover to guide the load, 
attempted to stop the lift. The plate dislodged and the rigger fell approximately 6.5 m to the deck below.
The injured person was medevaced with serious injuries. The event had clear fatality potential.

While parking the starboard (STBD) crane following routine lifting operations, the crane boom was brought down 
into the boom rest abruptly rather than in a controlled manner. This sudden placement generated an unexpected 
impact load on the crane structure, producing a loud bang that was heard in the vicinity of the crane pedestal and 
surrounding areas.
The abrupt motion and resulting impact load may have introduced a shock event into the crane’s hydraulic or 
electrical systems. A process shutdown occurred minutes after this impact, and although the causal link has not yet 
been fully established, the timing suggests the crane event may have contributed to or triggered the shutdown.

Contractor carrying out repairs on the Scale Inhibitor Injection system, the system was understood to have been 
depressurised. As the contractor started to release an end cap, the cap was projected downwards under pressure. 
The cap went directly downwards into a section of plant close to a walkway. This could have had potential to impact 
personnel.

Flex Joint strikes handrail creating 2 Dropped Objects. During the removal of the Flex Joint from the Riser Feeding 
Machine (RFM) using the starboard crane, the aft sling of the Flex Joint became hung up on the RFM bucket. As the 
lift continued, the sling suddenly released, causing the Flex Joint to swing unexpectedly.
The uncontrolled movement resulted in the Flex Joint striking and damaging the RFM track and the associated 
emergency-stop device. The Flex Joint then continued its swing path until coming to rest against the starboard-side 
handrail.
The impact dislodged two sections of the handrail, weighing 2.4 kg and 4.6 kg, corresponding to 377 Joules and 722 
Joules of potential energy respectively. Both handrail sections fell approximately 16 metres to the Riser Deck below.

Operator observed a concrete block on the tray of a flatbed truck and attempted to pick it up with the Front-end 
Loader tynes (pallet forks). The operator misjudged the fork tyne pockets of the pallet the concrete block was sitting 
on and inadvertently pushed the concrete block off the side of the flatbed truck. 
The concrete block weighed ~1.3 tonne and fell ~1.4m before rolling onto its side and coming to rest on the ground 
near a container on the opposite side of the flatbed truck.

During pallet racking activities in the warehouse, a forklift was in the process of lifting a pallet to the third shelf. The 
load backrest of the forklift inadvertently contacted another pallet directly above (load approximately 240kg) stored 
on the fourth shelf which dislodged and fell approximately 5.6m to grade. No personnel were injured. There was one 
nearby person 7 meters away.

IP1 observed visible bulging of a drain hose and proceeded to disconnect it. Although the associated compressor 
had been isolated, the hose remained connected to the main drainage manifold, which was linked to 24 
compressors.
The hose remained pressurized, and upon disconnection it struck the IP1 on the left hand and lower leg, and 
subsequently impacting IP2’s hand as they attempted to assist. As a result, IP1 and IP2 were injured.

Whilst departing the north berth of the supply base wharf, the contractor inspection maintenance repair vessel 
began moving starboard and aft whilst the forward fender was being lifted and recovered using the vessel’s crane.

ASIA/AUSTRALASIA ONSHORE

A crew member stepped out of a cherry picker while connecting a hydraulic hose to the Annular BOP, lost balance, 
and fell onto the cellar-pit grating. Subsequent hospital evaluation confirmed a left zygomatic bone fracture.
2-7/8" tubing was released from the lifting cap and hit the back of the right shoulder.

During hot work activities to replace process lines, the flange of a service water line was broken. This resulted in a 
release of water followed by a hydrocarbon/water emulsion. There was no CO/LEL detected and the material was 
removed by flushing with service water. Despite a very minor, intermittent liquid release (droplets) from the open 
line, work activities continued to cut an upstream service water line. About 10-15 minutes later, a fire ignited from 
the open process nozzle.
Fly jib on mobile crane fell to the floor.

Whilst lifting a pennant on deck as part of a lifting activity (~56.2m length, static weight 16.2 mT), a tagline was in 
a basket arrangement around the rigging to provide stability. The tagline had a single wrap on the generator lifting 
frame, used as an anchor point. During the lift, the involved person who had been on deck dogging the load in a safe 
location, moved to a location positioned between the generator and stored deck boards.
As the generator tilted, it trapped the involved person against a stack of wooden deck boards. The involved person 
received an injury that required Medevac to an onshore medical facility for further treatment.
Employee fell into well cellar.
Cut through live supply line.

When filling a mud tank with brine to prepare for cleaning of the tank, the transfer hose became dislodged, fell 
towards the ground (2.6m) and began to whip. The hose struck the pump operator’s leg, who suffered a ruptured 
Achilles tendon. The operator required surgery, classifying this as a Lost Work Day Case under IOGP guidelines. The 
incident is considered high potential, as the heavy hose coupling could have caused a fatality if it struck the head of 
the injured person when it fell.

On 8 October 2025 on an offshore rig, a lifting operation was underway to land an 11.8 m, 2.67 ton bottom hole 
assembly (BHA) into a storage basket on the riser deck. During the final positioning, the BHA made a sudden 
uncontrolled movement. The forward end either contacted the basket edge, rotating the load toward the injured 
person, or the crane made an unintended movement. The injured person was positioned in a narrow space between 
riser guide posts with no escape route available. He had earlier climbed onto adjacent baskets and manually guided 
the load several times to open covers in the inner basket. The BHA struck him in the chest and compressed him 
against another basket. Emergency response was immediate, and medical evacuation was carried out via search 
and rescue (SAR) helicopter. The investigation identified multiple human, organisational, technical, and task-related 
contributors including lack of hands-free lifting, trainee crane operator without supervision, congested deck layout, 
communication challenges, inadequate planning, and procedural non-compliance.

An operator was removing a grating panel with manual handling hooks on the weather deck. 
During the operation, the grating unhooked from the manual handling tools and fell through the opening, hit a cable 
gate before landing on the underlying deck, approximately 10 meters below. The grating measures 1x1 meter and 
weighs 52,4 kg which gives a kinetic energy of 5149, 44 Joules. No one was injured, but under slightly changed 
circumstances people could have been in the line of fire as the deck was not cordoned off and there was a work 
team close to the area where it dropped.
A worker was seriously injured when he fell from a height of 4.4 metres.
Sucker rod broke consequently elevator dropped.

During platform crane lifting operations to land a container on the main deck North landing, the IP sustained 
a crush/impact injury to shoulder/ribs. The crane and container were made safe and the individual treated by 
platform advanced first aider followed by coastguard medevac for further assessment.
Loss of Primary Containment – Methanol Release.
Jack failed, with load moving towards personnel. No injuries however fatality as worst case potential outcome.

Scaffold pole dropped to deck during handling operations. No injuries however dropped object calculator indicates 
fatality as worst case potential outcome.

A forklift driver’s ankle was struck by a spreader bar during offloading from a truck at the logistics base. There 
were no lifting pockets welded onto the bar. In past lifting operations, the spreader bar had been placed on wooden 
blocks on the truck bed and lifted directly on the forks of a forklift. This time the wooden blocks were not in place. 
The truck driver and the forklift driver decided to lift the spreader bar off the truck by hooking hoisting slings 
attached to the spreader bar and to the forklift forks, crossing them to reduce the length of the slings. During 
hoisting, the spreader bar rotated and swung into the forklift cabin, hitting the driver’s ankle. The forklift cabin door 
had been left open to improve communication between the drivers.

On an offshore drilling rig, on 1 September 2025, personnel and marine crew were installing handrails on top of a 
unit on the main deck. Handrail sections (60–90 kg) were lifted by deck crane to the top of the unit, where an operator 
worked at height to receive and install them, using fall-arrest equipment. The operator initially attached his lanyard 
to the stairs, then to handrail, and later to another section to reach the final corner section. To fit the last section, he 
had to lift and adjust some of the handrail. The locking pins were weakly retained and the chain/carabiner secondary 
securing arrangement did not prevent them from sliding out. The section of the handrail tilted and fell, pulling the 
operator with it. He fell approximately 4.3 m to deck, landing partly on the fallen handrail. The incident resulted in an 
LTI and a dropped object with calculated energy of 2733 J, with assessed potential for a single fatality.

In connection with a pigging operation on an offshore installation, several pigs weighing 35 - 40 kg were lowered 
from a scaffold using rope, as the pig receiver was placed 5m above the turret deck. When the last pig was being 
lowered, the knot loosened, and the pig fell onto the turret deck and then bounced outside the barrier and down 
onto the tank deck. No one was injured and there was no significant material damage.
Collision between northern crane and derrick resulting in falling objects.

Two personnel experienced symptoms of severe oxygen deficiency during inspection work, but managed to self-
evacuate safely. Subsequent measurements confirmed low oxygen levels inside the enclosure, linked to nitrogen 
ingress from the turbine seal system combined with a lack of ventilation.

During preparations for installing a 20’’ sealing ring on the platform on 2 July 2025, a technician tested the ring 
for fit before the lift operation. The 7.1 kg ring slipped from the technician’s hands and fell 6.35 meters to the deck 
below, landing approximately two meters from a mechanic who was grinding at deck level. The ring then bounced 
and struck the mechanic on the arm. The mechanic received a first-aid level impact with no observable injury. The 
event had a severe potential for fatality due to the weight and fall height. The ring had been brought into the elevated 
work area earlier than planned, the area was insufficiently barricaded, and the test occurred without notification to 
the crew below. Multiple procedural, communication and barrier-management weaknesses contributed.
Gangway disconnect during personnel transfer.

During the night shift, the crew attempted to release an anchor latch tool from a permanent packer using a straight 
pull of 60 klbs (including 55 klbs string weight) without success. Following contractors’ procedures, the string 
was tensioned with 5 klbs over string weight and rotated manually, but no movement was observed. Based on 
contractors’ instructions, power tongs were partially used due to the absence of a power swivel on site.
During the sixth right-hand turn with a 5 klbs overpull, the 2-7/8" tubing coupling connected to the safety valve backed 
off and fell approximately 21 ft onto the rig floor, then a further 14 ft to the ground. At the same time, the tubing string 
settled approximately 6 ft into the packer. The combined weight of the coupling and safety valve was 36.5 kg.

While dismantling a scaffold, a contractor accidentally dropped a scaffold board. The board struck a 0.5-inch, 32-bar 
pressurized tube, causing physical damage to the tube and resulting in a gas leak.

During maintenance activities, an electrical arc occurred in Switch Rack 6 LV, resulting in electrical burns to two 
electrical technicians. The injured personnel received immediate evacuation to the clinic for initial medical attention 
before being transferred to the Hospital for further treatment.

A contractor working in the Telecoms room at Central Control Building was found removing a light fixture from the 
ceiling without ensuring the power was fully isolated. The light was part of an energized circuit, switched off only at 
the local lighting switch. With the light removed, the exposed flex had bare copper ends, live and hanging from the 
ceiling. The worker, on metal steps, was at risk of electrocution if someone had entered and switched on the lights

Observed that a Contractor Scaffolder working at 12m height on a Piperack without using his fall protection, 
standing on the hanging scaffold platform without using his double lanyards attached to a suitable anchor point and 
there was no handrail in place for fall prevention.

A Contractor scaffolder was dismantling a scaffold by removing a 3m high scaffold standard at a height of 11.5m, 
without using lanyards and passing the scaffold standard to a colleague below.

A forklift operator was pulling a service hose from the backyard to the rig location, the operator raised the boom 
to a higher position. During this operation, the boom came into contact with a deadline data cable positioned 
approximately 5 meters high on overhead line stands. As a result, the cable fell and sustained minor damage. There 
were no injuries or harm to personnel

During space-out of the traveling block to function-test the power tong, the Driller hoisted the traveling block with 
the working string. When the string was about 2 meters above the rig floor, the Driller applied the brake. At that 
moment, the traveling block and working string suddenly moved down to the rig floor. Work string landed on the slip 
and travelling block stopped moving where the brake was activated.

A contractor mechanical field service representative and mechanical team had disconnected the export gas 
compressor gas turbine’s primary and secondary flexible fuel gas hoses. After disconnecting the hoses, the 
contractor field service representative was on the back side of the gas turbine while the mechanical technicians 
were on the front side. While lying beneath the gas turbine to check the water wash drain tube under the gas 
turbine, pressure was released, causing the loose hoses to swing.
Company pickup truck collided with a concrete barrier at a diversion point.

A steel structure crew was modifying a permanent grating platform handrail when a crowbar (weight approximately 
0.72kg) fell from the platform (height 20 metres) and landed on the ground below in an unbarricaded area. No 
person injury occurred or was reported.

A gate door (two sections) of the Blasting Shop toppled over due to strong winds (approximately 16m/s). Each door 
section measures 7.5m x 4m and weighs approx. 425kg. They landed on the ground and came to rest on a pipe 
stand, resulting in damage to the cladding and frame. The incident occurred next to a pedestrian walkway, but no 
personnel were in the vicinity at the time. No personal Injury was reported

A trailer driver was transporting six concrete barriers (3.5t each) on a flatbed trailer. The barriers were stacked in 
two rows (three in each row), with one cargo lashing belt securing two concrete barriers each. While the trailer was 
travelling on the bumpy road, the driver noticed that one of the lashing belts securing the rear concrete barriers 
had broken, causing the load to shift slightly towards the edge of the trailer. He pulled over to address the situation. 
Fortunately, no injuries or damage occurred.

During welding activities, the fire watch for the naked flame activity received an electrical shock when attempting to 
shift an electrical welding rod oven.

A telehandler operator was moving a 714kg pipe spool when he observed a trailer blocking his access. The operator 
pulled the telehandler over to the side waiting for the trailer to move away. When the trailer moved, the operator 
started to reverse the telehandler. After reversing approximately 2 metres, the front right tyre of the telehandler 
failed and exploded. The release of pressure ejected the tyre 7 metres away from the telehandler. The primary 
locking rim (weight 19.3kg) and the secondary locking rim (weight 2.3kg) were ejected from the split rim, causing 
the primary locking rim to land 50 metres away and the secondary locking rim to land 70 metres away. No injuries 
were reported. The Flagman and Rigger were positioned behind the telehandler approximately 5 metres away.

An 800-ton crawler crane and a 280-ton crawler crane had concluded lifting operations and were idle. A civil crew 
requested the 800-ton crane operator to reposition the hook so they could avoid working under it. While slewing, the 
boom tip section of the 800-ton crawler crane contacted the wire rope of the stationary 280-ton crawler crane. The 
crane was operating within a barricaded area. No visible damage was found on both crawler cranes, and there were 
no injuries

While a Wellhead Engineer was installing a side outlet valve at the wellhead deck, a Floor Man was preparing 
downhole guides on the upper deck level, but one down hole guide clamp, weighing 7 kg, slipped and dropped 
through open hatch and hit the right middle side of the hard hat above the brim and landed in the grating, causing 
the IP to fall on to the grating resulting in bruises to his right forehead and injury to his right knee.
Power cable damage during excavation.

Workers were unloading sandbags from the bucket of a wheel loader. While unloading the sandbags, a worker’s left 
foot was under the loader’s bucket. The bucket was inadvertently lowered, resulting in a crush injury to the worker 
(hereinafter referred to as the injured person or IP).

On 30/04/2025, a High Potential (HIPO) occurred when a crane’s counterweight of 15 tonnes fell off the trailer due 
to failure in the securing belt. The trailer was moving from the laydown area to the well-pad. No personnel injuries 
were reported.

After completing the second gyro survey, the crew began rigging down. On the platform deck, a tugger line was 
attached to the gyro tool as secondary retention. The tool was lifted to the rig floor using the wireline. Once above 
the rotary table, the wireline gooseneck was installed on top of the tool. As the tugger was spooled in to take the 
tool’s weight, its swivel caught the gooseneck, pulling it off. The gooseneck, weighing 2.3 kg, fell approximately 50 ft 
from the rotary table to the platform deck.

During racking-back a 7” landing joint using the Monkey board forward pullback tugger, the line parted, causing 
the parted hook and line to fall from the Monkey board to the rig floor. No one was injured or struck by the dropped 
object. 3 crew members were in the Red Zone at the time of the Dropped Object. Hook weighed 0.75kg and dropped 
83ft approx.

The rig crew were in the process of nipple down the bell nipple mandrel. While positioning the multi purpose crane 
for installing the bell nipple lifting slings the man basket (354kg), which was holding 2 persons, dislodged from the 
main structure of the crane and fell approx.16.5m to the top deck of the platform. Neither of the 2 persons fell as 
they were suspended by their harness and inertia reels. Both personnel were recovered in 2 minutes. One of the 2 
personnel received first aid treatment for slight swelling.

During the workboat transfer operation, workboat was transferred from the laydown area to the transport vessel 
main deck and positioned in its transport cradle. During final positioning, the vessel could not remain steady. As a 
result, the workboat swung into a nearby Cargo Carrying Unit (CCU), causing damage to the hull. A crew member 
handling a tag line was exposed to risk and was nearly caught between the CCU and the swinging workboat.

Two project contractors were observed working outside the handrail on structural beams approximately 30 meters 
above sea level. They were without the required fall-prevention barriers or authorized permits. Both individuals 
faced an uncontrolled fall-from-height hazard, posing a significant risk where survivability is minimal and multiple 
fatalities could occur.

IP was working alone and attempted to disconnect a 2" airline which was pressurized. An assumption was made 
that line was de-pressurized without being verified - line was still connected to an air compressor. Upon release, 
hose kicked back striking IPs hand and helmet.

On May 20, 2025, a worker was engaged in repositioning a spec blind from the closed to the open position on the 
flare line, in preparation to de-isolate the unit for commissioning activities. During this activity, the worker was 
exposed to a gas/energy release from the down steam side of the isolated gate valve at the open flange pair. Worker 
required rescue from heights and was provided onsite first aid; worker was transported to a local hospital for 
further medical assessment where it was determined worker sustained bruised ribs and a concussion. Worker was 
released from hospital the same day.

During a fluid-hauling task, water transfer to a tank truck was completed and the hose was disconnected. A valve 
was found not fully closed, and hot fluid sprayed during subsequent valve manipulation. The job was stopped, 
emergency medical response was initiated, and the well/site was shut down to support response and control the 
release.

During offloading of a delivery of structural steel, a stacked load became unstable while the final securement strap 
was being removed. A beam fell from the trailer and struck a worker. Emergency response was initiated, the beam 
was removed from contact, and the worker was transported for medical assessment and treatment.

Crew was killing the well with Axis Reverse Unit when the Axis Pump Hand appears to have engaged valves in 
the incorrect order allowing pressure to exit well bore through a disconnected 2” hose at the rig floor. Pressure 
estimated to be 600 psi. Loose end of hose whipped and struck one individual on the top of their hard hat.

A Mechanic and an E-Tech were repairing a section of the natural gas manifold on frac pump. The employees were 
replacing a section on the manifold referred to as a pistol. After the repairs were made the employees opened 
the natural gas supply valve to supply the gas manifold on the pump. The mechanic stepped up onto a platform to 
open the main ball valve of the natural gas manifold to allow the pump to start burning the natural gas as fuel. As 
the mechanic (IP) opened the main ball valve, both employees heard a loud pop noise. The top of the low-pressure 
regulator (VDR) broke away from its base and struck the mechanic in the head above his right eye causing a 
laceration. The top of the VDR is made of aluminum and weighs approximately 1lb/~454g. The IP was evaluated at a 
local emergency room, and the IP received 8 sutures to close the laceration.
IP contacted by 2 3/8" joint of pipe.

A flash fire occurred during the demolition of internal components in the first-stage knockout drum (module C2) at 
the facility.

While releasing the tubing hanger, after a BOP test, unknown pressure had built up below the tubing hanger 
assembly causing it to lift up out of the BOP stack and fall to the ground.

While changing out tong heads during an ESP install, the IP’s right arm came into contact with the actuating lever, 
activating the tongs. IP’s left forearm was struck by the rotation of the tongs.

A worker fell approximately 16 feet from an aerial work platform onto a Christmas tree cart. The incident occurred 
while the worker was using a rope tied to the basket to pull an umbilical and create slack for a storm loop. The rope 
failed under tension, releasing stored energy that transferred to the basket. This sudden release caused the basket 
to jolt, ejecting the worker.

While adjusting the ultra-high-pressure water blasting equipment in close proximity to normally energized cable 
trays, in three separate instances, two workers reported experiencing electrical shock sensations upon contacting 
the cable trays.

Following heavy rainfall, landslide occurred in the area behind the ten wagon-type cabins (accommodation, canteen, 
washing, changing, and rest facilities) located at the oil well site. A ground instability and multiple surface cracks 
were identified in the surrounding area.
Personnel were immediately informed of the hazardous ground conditions and instructed to remain vigilant and 
exercise caution.
As a preventive control measure, the wagon-type units were relocated to a safer area to eliminate the risk of impact 
from further ground movement.

Contractor personnel were performing a scheduled calibration of a flow meter in accordance with the preventive 
maintenance plan.
During the calibration process, the technician initiated pressure stabilization by draining fluid through the 
designated drainage line. To enhance the drainage process, the technician also opted to use an additional line and 
proceeded to remove the plug at the end of that line.
Upon removal of the plug, an uncontrolled release of oil containing H2S occurred. Work was stopped immediately. 
Workers H2S detectors activated, donned respirators and evacuated the area.

A dropped object incident occurred while lowering an overdrive with the casing joint held stationary in the elevator. 
The mud saver (component of overdrive) contacted top of the liner joint in the rotary, causing failure at the 
connection to the mandrel. The mud saver (~40 kg) fell ~14 meters to the rig floor.
Two personnel were in the red zone at the time (required for the task).

During the installation of a subsea telescopic clamp on the well shaft beneath the offshore platform, the Diving 
Service team encountered a safety-critical situation when a support vessel unexpectedly approached the platform, 
despite all established safety measures being in place. The vessel’s captain was promptly contacted and informed 
that underwater diving operations were in progress.

During the inspection of the 8-inch subsea oil and gas pipeline located between offshore platforms, diving 
operations were in progress and a scheduled descent from the diving vessel had commenced.
Approximately 15 minutes after the diver entered the water, the vessel’s mechanic reported hull damage resulting in 
water ingress into the engine room.
The diver was immediately recovered from the water, and the vessel proceeded toward the platform, where it was 
safely moored at the docking bridge.
Following the safe disembarkation of personnel, the damaged vessel was towed to the onshore port by an assisting 
tugboat.
While performing orifice change on a choke valve, the choke bean was ejected toward the operator´s position.

Contractor personnel were working on the installation of a 12-inch spool at ground level, while it was being held 
in a lifting operation. For causes yet to be determined, an actuated valve (SDV) located near the installation area - 
resting vertically on the ground and not involved in the lifting operation - lost its vertical stability and fell, resulting 
in a person being crushed between the valve and the skid structure.

Crew shuttle collision during a braking manoeuvre, the shuttle initially collided with the vehicle in front, then 
crossed into the oncoming lane and was struck on the right side by a semi-trailer truck traveling in the opposite 
direction.

During the movement of the workover rig truck from one well to another, the rear tyre on one of the truck’s axles 
completely detached, resulting in an impact with the injection line of a well, with no visible damage.

During the dismantling of scaffolding in a 45° angular configuration, assembler 01 had to apply excessive force 
to loosen a remaining clamp (exposed to the weather) using a ratchet wrench, causing the bolt to shear and 
subsequently break. With the sudden opening of the clamp, the tube (3.65 kg) slipped from his left hand, fell, and 
slid along the structure, traveling a lateral distance of approximately 4.5 meters, striking the back of assembler 04s 
helmet on the lower level, resulting in a superficial cut to the scalp.

During maintenance work at a Generation Unit, the mechanical technician suffered a fall from height, falling to a 
lower level from the engine access platform.

During the heating of an 18-inch pipe to remove the coating, the worker placed the torch at the entrance of the 18-
inch pipe. When attempting to light the torch with a manual spark igniter, a flammable atmosphere was created, 
causing a flash fire that resulted in first and second-degree burns to the worker's face after being hit sideways by a 
flash fire in the manufacturing workshop area.

During production tubing running operations on the drilling rig, four metallic components fell from height while 
using the catline system.
• Objects dropped from approximately 40 m height
• 2 × 1.8 kg (≈ 706 J each)

width of the platform, spanning from one side to the other. As a result, access to the muster location necessarily 
required personnel to pass through the flammable gas cloud.
The tanks were depressurized both through the fully open dome, which was already providing an unrestricted 
release path, and by remotely opening the vent stacks. Despite these depressurization measures, the uncontrolled 
release continued for nearly one hour, until the tanks were fully vented and pressure equalized with the atmosphere.

halted, and personnel were exposed to significant risk due to the prolonged presence of a flammable atmosphere 
across the installation.

the morning of the incident, this last active pipeline ruptured after years of progressive corrosion, which developed 
specifically on its upper surface - an area exposed to salty water dripping through an unsealed opening between 
decks directly above. Because the line was installed in an elevated position, the most recent inspections did not fully 
address the upper side, allowing a localized, severe corrosion spot on the top of the pipe to go undetected. When the 
rupture finally occurred, a large volume of flammable gas was released and quickly ignited, resulting in a powerful 
jet fire and vapor cloud explosion. Multiple workers were injured, rescue efforts were hampered by equipment 
failures and communication problems, and the event resulted in significant material damage and evacuation of the 
platform.

The employee stepped back into the cellar opening and fell 4 feet down onto a metal work platform and toe board, resulting in a broken collar bone, broken ribs, and a punctured lung.

On the morning of July 21, 2022, two employees were at a stacked rig, removing 4-inch high-pressure piping. They began to break the nuts loose on the saddle clamp bolts under the valve tree. As they were breaking loose the last nut, the piping suddenly rotated in the saddle clamp and the transducer valve tree (about 4 feet tall, weighing 250 pounds) pivoted 90 degrees toward the ground and landed on one of the employees. The hammer union ears at the top of the valve tree struck him in the middle of the shoulder and back, causing contusions.
An employee was doing welding work on a cylinder. The cylinder fell from a skid frame. As the employee went to catch it, it partially amputated the bottom of his left middle finger.
An employee was working in an area with an open-ended line when hot steam/water splashed on his back.
An employee was moving a large job site tool. The tool fell and caught his right hand resulting in amputation of the pinky fingertip.

An employee was steadying a road boring machine as it was loaded onto the back of a truck. The employee's right index finger was in a pinch point when the machine was lowered onto the finger, crushing it and requiring a medical amputation.
During routine maintenance of the bonnet end cap on a blowout preventer, the cap fell and smashed an employee's right ring finger against another ram bonnet. The finger was amputated.

An employee was working to set a drive pin on an S-hook so a forklift could pick up a part and bring it to the paint department. The employee's left middle finger was pinched between the pin and the S-hook resulting in a partial amputation.

An employee was watching the landing joint being lowered into the rotary table when it clipped the slip bowl, causing the slip bowl to flip over and strike the employee's legs. The employee's right femur was fractured and they sustained a fracture to the left leg below the knee. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was troubleshooting a compressor that had shut down. The employee believed that a 1-inch choke nipple was plugged and drained fluids via the dump line to check the choke nipple. The employee then loosened a union and a flash fire occurred, burning the employee's hands and face.
An employee was working on the controller drive for the down hole equipment when he received an electrical shock, resulting in burns to the right thumb and left forearm and face.

While working at a fueling station, an employee was inside an underground sump hole with safety cones blocking off the area. He stood up in preparation to get out of the hole when a truck drove over the hole. The wheel of the vehicle was stuck in the hole and trapped the employee against the inside of the hole, putting pressure on the employee's upper torso.

An employee removed a blow out preventer (BOP) from a well head. The BOP was suspended by the rig. While suspended, the BOP started rotating catching the employee's left ring fingertip between the BOP and the stationary well head resulting in amputation.

An employee was working on the ground aligning the bottom of a 13 3/8" casing joint into the drilling rig v-door by hand. A winch on the rig floor was lifting the joint top through the v-door. The winch line was lowered causing the bottom of the pipe to slide into the injured employee's left foot resulting in a compound ankle fracture.

An employee was offloading asphalt from a truck to a tank. As the system was pressurized, hot asphalt struck the employee in the face and chest. The employee suffered burns to the face and chest, as well as a broken sternum and ribs. The employee was hospitalized.
On July 17, 2925, an employee was working on a computer inside a vehicle when they began experiencing symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning, resulting in hospitalization.
An employee was injured when condensate spontaneously released while the employee was starting up a coker.
An employee was walking in packed snow when the employee slipped and fell to the ground, suffering a fractured right femur.
While loading water from a pipeline into a trailer, an employee was struck by a pipeline pig that ejected out of the pipeline. The employee suffered a broken ankle and leg.

On February 19, 2017, an employee slid down a containment mat and struck a pressure gauge on the wellhead while attempting to pull slack in a wire line. He suffered a rib injury that required hospitalization.
An employee was mixing mud when he began to feel dizzy due to dehydration from the heat.

An employee was attempting to adjust the housing on the tip of a spray gun when the trigger was engaged, causing the ceramic coating to go through the employee's glove into his left index finger, resulting in an injury that required surgery.

At the facility shop area, an employee tripped over his feet and fell on an industrial sized valve stem used in hydrofracking (a piece of sharp equipment) and lacerated his abdomen. This injury required hospitalization for two days.

The sheaves of the crane were frozen due to ice and snow conditions, which caused a backlash with the auxiliary cable of the crane. The operator attempted to straighten out the backlash on the superstructure near the drum. The frozen sheave freed itself, allowing the cable to run, and the operator's right arm got tangled in the cable. The operator sustained an open fracture of the humerus and a dislocation of the radius.

An employee had unstrapped some downhole tools that were brought to a wellsite. While another employee was going to get a forklift, the load shifted and smashed his finger between the load and the rub rail, resulting in a finger amputation.

Two employees were removing residual hot mix asphalt with a torch inside a silo before mixing a new batch of asphalt. The asphalt became hot enough to ignite fumes inside the silo, which resulted in a flash fire. Both employees sustained burns to their hands, arms, and face.
On 11/16/2017, two employees were attempting to clear a hydrate formation in a gas pipeline at a tank battery when flammable gases and vapors ignited, causing significant burns to both employees.
An employee was working on the rig floor when a traveling block fell and struck him, fracturing his clavicle and ribs.

An employee was driving an all-terrain vehicle to inspect a well. The vehicle struck an uneven surface, ejecting the employee from the vehicle to the ground. The employee sustained bilateral leg fractures.

An employee was helping an operator to pull a cable off a winch. The operator pulled in the line when it hooked some tree brush. The brush then whipped around and struck the employee's arm, resulting in a broken arm.
An employee was working on a crew, installing and pressure-testing PVC lines for a sewage line. The PVC pipe struck the employee's face, causing severe damage.

An employee was dumping a mini dumpster, mounted on a forklift, into a large trash container. When the mini dumpster tipped, the employee's finger was caught between it and the forklift's forks. The employee's fingertip was amputated.

An employee was loading asphalt from a storage tank into a tanker truck from an above ground asphalt loading rack. After removing the loading spout from the tanker and placing a bucket drip pan under it, the employee stepped onto the crows nest of the truck to close the loading hatch. Residual asphalt (approximately 370 degrees F) in the loading line spilled out of the spout, into the bucket, and splashed down onto the employee below. The employee sustained second-degree burns to the back of his head, neck, ears, and side of his face near the jawline. The employee was hospitalized.

The injured employee was preparing samples for testing and was processing nitric acid and oil and gas samples in a glass container when the glass container exploded resulting in burns and puncture wounds to the employee's hands and arms.

On or about 3 June 2015, at approximately 1825 hours, an AR Daniel Construction employee was hospitalized due to an injury acquired at the jobsite. The employee was working in a trench under the railroad tracks located at Grand and 3rd street in Amarillo, Texas, when he was struck in the face by a piece of angle iron that was being used to hoist the pipeline that he was working near. The angle iron was inside the pipe, and a line was tied to the angle iron to hoist the pipe up enough for the employee to remove wood planking from underneath it. The angle iron became dislodged and struck him, causing multiple facial fractures and lacerations.
An employee was on a ladder welding when a piece of slag fell onto his sweater which caught fire. The employee sustained burns to the upper body.
An employee was operating a forklift at a well site and was hospitalized for heat stress.

Employees at an oil rig were breaking down its blowout preventers. After removing the preventers from the wellhead, they put a wooden board on the ground to set the preventer on and keep it from getting muddy. When one employee unhooked his tagline from a preventer, the preventer shifted and the locking stem on its top struck the top of the employee's left boot. He suffered a laceration to the foot and two broken toes.
An employee was walking through an open area when high winds caused a crane boom to collapse. Debris struck the employee and broke the employee's right tibia and left foot.

An employee was completing a fluid treatment process. The employee had just closed a 4-inch valve on a "T" manifold when he tripped and fell forward, striking the shin of his right leg against a valve handle and then landing on the ground. The employee's right leg sustained a spiral fracture requiring hospitalization and surgery.

On or about 7/6/16, at 17:45 hours, an employee had been working outside at several oilfield locations in high heat conditions when he began feeling ill and collapsed. He was hospitalized for heat exhaustion.

An employee was walking toward a pump on which he was installing a new suction manifold. He tripped over the old manifold, lying on the ground, and fell. He suffered a compound fracture to the left forearm and was hospitalized.

On May 4, 2023, an employee was cutting a catwalk platform with a torch. When the pressure released, the platform fell back toward the employee and knocked him off his feet. The platform then landed on his leg, resulting in a fracture.
An employee was resetting a breaker on an electric motor when an electrical arc occurred resulting in burns to the employee's right ear, right hand, thumb, and index finger.

On 1/21/15 at about 16:20 pm a worker was hit by the tongs on his right arm, chest, and leg. He was transported to OU Medical Center where his right hand was amputated. Immediately before the accident the drilling line was stuck. The snub line connected to the tongs snapped causing the tongs to swing around and hit the worker.

An employee was climbing a ladder with guard rails to access the rig floor. The ladder twisted to one side causing the employee to fall to the ground. The employee sustained displaced vertebrae in the neck and bruising and soreness.
An employee was welding a tank battery in the field when the welding torch ignited flammable gasses, causing an explosion that resulted in second and third degree burns to both hands and their face.
An employee slipped and fell to the ground while exiting a water truck via the ladder. The employee was hospitalized for a foot/ankle injury.

An employee was blowing off pressure on a field natural gas compressor when a pipe about 3 feet long pulled out of the threads and hit the employee, causing blunt force trauma to the face, arm, and shoulder.

An employee was pushing the forks of a forklift to widen their position. He needed to get the forks around the hook it sits in. Once it cleared the hook, the fork slid quickly, catching the employee's right middle finger against the headache rack support. The finger was amputated.

After running a survey and putting air back on the hole, two employees were standing in the doorway of the doghouse watching the flow line to see if there was a gas flare. The pilot light for the flow line was not ignited. The injured employee used a propane torch to igniting the pilot light. A flash fire resulted due to down-hole gas that had come out of the flow line. The injured employee sustained second degree burns to their face, forearms, and hands.
An employee tripped going over a containment curb and fell. A Unistrut clip caused a laceration and degloving injury to his abdomen.
On July 22, 2017, an employee was hooking up a holiday detector to scan a pipe for any bare metal when he received an electrical shock on the hand and fell to the ground. He was hospitalized.
An employee was putting a pipe in place and pushing on a rotating sucker rod, which caught his glove and wrapped his arm around the rod. The employee sustained multiple arm fractures.

An employee was about to change out the choke parts to fix a leaking choke on the belly dump of a gas production unit (GPU). While the choke was being unbolted, pressure came through it, blowing the employee backward and causing lacerations and broken bones in their face.

Employees were lowering material into a dumpster using a digger derrick truck. The injured employee jumped into the dumpster to remove a strap from the pallet. Their right tibia was fractured when their leg contacted the bottom of the dumpster.

A skid steer operator was attaching a skid steer's bucket loaded with concrete (estimated to be up to 500 pounds) to a machine. The injured employee was reaching in front of the bucket to move pieces of broken concrete when the bucket fell on his right arm, catching it between the bucket and concrete. The employee sustained a fractured arm and thumb, a laceration to the index finger, and an avulsion to their middle finger.

An employee was standing on planking located on the top buck of a two-end frame, tubular-welded frame scaffold when one of the scaffold planks broke, causing the employee to fall 10 feet to the ground below. The employee suffered a fractured hip and two fractured ribs.
An employee was repairing a flow pipe when he tripped and fell backward with the flow pipe on his body. He fractured his left ankle.

An employee was about to climb a 15-foot chain ladder to exit a horizontal vessel. When he stepped onto the ladder, it became unstable and he fell. He landed on his back on the vessel's floor, suffering multiple broken vertebrae.

A crew of two was attempting to blind/isolate the loop to the re-slurry control valve to the north rise. As the employees were loosening the bolts to open the pipe and placing the blind, a valve that was holding back the slurry opened. This released the hot slurry (640 degrees Fahrenheit) onto the employees performing the work. Both employees sustained thermal burns from the slurry and were hospitalized.

Three employees were removing a cover from an oil well storage tank. Some of the bolts were corroded, so the employees used an electric grinder to remove the bolts. Sparks from the grinding wheel ignited liquid/fumes inside the tank, causing the tank to explode. One employee received severe burns to over 70% of their body.
An employee was replacing the valve on a frac pump. Fingers on his left hand were caught in the pump's moving pistons and injured; the middle finger required surgery.
An employee was walking up the steps to shut off a sprayer when he fell from the steps. The employee injured his right heel and fractured his left tibia and was hospitalized.
An oil derrick hand fell off the oil derrick platform and struck the derrick during the fall resulting in a fractured back.

An employee was under the rig floor adjusting a chain on the slips when his finger became caught between the chain and the blowout preventer (BOP). The employee sustained the amputation of his finger.

An employee was checking fluid levels on a mast/power pack unit. The employee was on a ladder trying to access a catwalk when they slipped on a wet rung and fell 5 feet to the ground. The employee sustained a fractured hip.

An employee was troubleshooting a problem with a chemical pump. During a fracturing operation, the employee disconnected a chemical hose that was under pressure. Chemicals released and entered the employee's right eye, causing a chemical burn.

An employee was in a trench, welding/installing a new pipe that was being held up using an excavator. The excavator arm rotated, and the employee was pinned between the pipe and the trench box. The employee suffered three broken ribs and a collapsed lung.
An employee was attempting to climb up an angle iron piece of a substructure when he slipped and fell backward 4 feet to the ground, suffering a spiral fracture to his right ankle.

Two employees were moving 40-foot long pipes (30 inches in diameter and weighing over 1,000 lbs.) on an elevated pipe rack into the pipe coating facility. While moving the last pipe, one employee's right hand was caught between a stationary pipe and the moving pipe, partially amputating his right ring fingertip and avulsing his right long fingernail with a nailbed laceration. He was hospitalized overnight.
An employee slipped and fell on ice in the parking lot. He injured his knee and required surgery.

An employee was on the catwalk of a mixing plant at a completed well site. He was burned by a fire, centered on a forklift and a flowback tank that was releasing natural gas. He suffered second- and third-degree burns to his right hand and arm to the shoulder, his left hand, and his back on the right side. He also suffered second-degree burns to the right side of his face (excluding the eyes) and first-degree burns to his forehead. Personal protective equipment and flame-retardant pants were being worn, but not a flame-retardant shirt.

On or about 12 April 2015, at approximately 1410 hours, an employee amputated the distal portion of his left-hand, index phalanges (no bone involved). He was installing a hydraulic cylinder on a drilling rig when the cylinder he was holding swung laterally, pinching his distal phalanges between the cylinder and the drilling rig structure.
An employee was washing an oil and gas drilling rig when he experienced heat stress and cramping due to dehydration, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was guiding/lowering a Kelly hose off to the side of the work floor with a winch line when a counterweight slid down the winch line and struck the employee's left hand, causing an open fracture that required hospitalization.
An employee was removing nuts from a pump unit. The employee slipped and their right index fingertip was crushed between the pump and a rachet. The fingertip was amputated.
While tasked with checking inventory in the warehouse, an employee was stung on the left thigh by an insect. The employee was hospitalized.

Employees were cleaning a storage tank for petroleum. Employee 1 was inside the tank and employee 2 was outside the tank approximately 30 to 40 feet away when a flash fire occurred. The force of the fire/explosion threw employee 1 into a wall. Employee 1 sustained fractures to the left collar bone and left ribs, a dislocated right elbow, a lacerated left ear, and burns. Employee 2 sustained second-and-third- degree burns to the face, chest, hands, and fingers.

An employee was performing normal work duties doing a "meter run" when he started to feel badly and went to the Arnett office. Employees/management at that location thought the employee was suffering from heat related issues and called an ambulance. The employee was treated at the hospital for heat stress.

An employee and driver were unloading a frac tank from a winch truck. While trying to unhook the winch cable from the tank, the driver tightened the winch cable instead of loosening it, pinching the employee's finger between the cable and rear roller. The employee's right index fingertip was amputated.
An employee opened the hatch on an oil tank. The exposure to hydrogen sulfide and other gases caused the employee to become ill, dizzy, and lightheaded; the employee was hospitalized.

A dump truck was trying to avoid rocks on a trail when its left-side wheels left the trail. The truck rolled about three times, and the driver suffered a neck strain, bumps and bruises, a laceration to the forehead that required stitches, and a laceration to the right forearm.

A valve stem had been stood up against the blades of a forklift so an employee could take a measurement. It slid down the forklift fork, striking the employee's left hand and partially amputating the index fingertip.

An employee was removing a gasket from the top of the open hatch of a heater treater to make weir adjustments on the low pressure vessel when metal-on-metal contact caused a spark that ignited residual gasses. The employee sustained burns to their face, neck and hands.

An employee was assisting a rig crew with stabbing drill pipe into a rotating head. The employee's fingertips became caught between the rotating rubber head and a trip nipple causing lacerations to four fingertips on the left hand and partial amputations to his right ring and little fingers.
On February 17, 2021, an employee was completing rounds through a natural gas planet when he slipped and fell on an ice spot. He was hospitalized, having suffered a broken left hip.

An employee was standing on top of an excavation area flagging a trench box in when the ground gave way. The employee fell inside the trench, hitting the left side of his head and back, breaking four ribs, and bruising his head.
An employee was inventorying hammer mill screens when the screens fell on the employee. The employee sustained a laceration to their leg requiring hospitalization.
An employee was on a table trying to push a block of cardboard paper. The employee fell from the table to the ground about 3 feet below, suffering a broken leg.

An employee was at the side of a truck (a pulling unit) removing tools. As the pole on the unit was extended, the elevator came unclasped off the hook, fell, and struck the employee on the side of his head. He suffered a skull fracture.

An employee was tightening the packing bolts on a beam pumping unit in the oil field by using an air impact wrench when the head of the unit, while in a down stroke, came in contact with the impact wrench forcing it downward and mashing the tool against the left index finger. The employee sustained a partial amputation of the left index fingertip.
An employee tripped and twisted his ankle while stepping down from a machine. He suffered a displaced fracture to the right fibula and a sprained ligament in the right ankle.

An employee was greasing valves when he lost his footing and fell backward on a fluid pumping trailer. While he was falling, his right leg was caught in a 6-inch gap between the bumper and trailer, breaking his right fibula and tibia.

An employee was sitting on a haul trailer when an ATV backed into him pinning him against the haul trailer. The employee was hospitalized for a fractured right femur, a broken nose and a one-inch laceration on his right check.

An employee had just finished lifting a shale bin using two loaders (one with a stinger, chain, and lifting equipment) in order to place matting underneath. Once the matting was in place, the employee directed the loader to lower the bin until there was enough slack in the lifting chain to remove it. As the employee grabbed the eye of the lifting chain to unhook it, the operator of the loader bumped the controls with his knee, causing the chain to tighten and pinch the employee's right middle finger between the bin and the chain. The employee's right middle finger was amputated between the middle and upper joint, and the employee was hospitalized.
While using a tag line to move a pipe, an employee lost control of the tag line. The employee's right arm was then caught between the pipe and a drilling rig, breaking it.
An employee was welding a trailer fender. The tire burst and debris struck the welding mask causing a facial laceration and temporary vision impairment. The injured employee was hospitalized.

On September 07, 2016, at approximately 2:00 AM, an employee was unloading a fluid trailer during fluid service operations. While he was disconnecting a hose, pressure released and he fell to the ground, sustaining a head injury.

Employees were attempting to lift and move a cellar cover in order to install a work platform in the cellar for a welder. The cover came into contact with the blowout preventer spool, causing it to fall back. An employee's right middle finger was caught between the cellar cover and the tin horn, causing an amputation to the first knuckle.

An employee at a remote Marathon Oil jobsite was pressure testing pipe when he was struck-by 9500psi of water when bolts broke on the flange connecting two pipes causing the high pressure water to strike the employee and one other sub-contractor's employee who were standing approximately 15 feet away.
An employee was sprayed with 12.5 percent sodium hypochlorite when a line burst on a pumping unit. The employee suffered a chemical burn.
An employee was conducting field work at a customer's drilling rig when he became dehydrated. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was tripping out rods on a servicing rig when his hand was caught above the rod transfer case near the swivel. His right arm was then caught and fractured on the rod transfer.

An employee was transferring diesel fuel from a 4,500 gallon fuel transport wagon to a semi-truck. Diesel fuel vapors and static caused an explosion/fire, resulting in burns to the employee's face and upper torso.
An employee was working on the rig floor. Equipment fell to the rig floor and the employee jumped off the rig onto the ground suffering a compound fracture to the right ankle.

An employee was standing behind a winch truck. The truck rolled back and ran over the employee's left leg. The employee suffered a thigh injury, a head laceration, and bruising to the right-side ribs.

An employee was redressing a compact setting tool and had it in a vise. He put the mandrel in the sleeve and attempted to screw the mandrel onto the tool. When he let go of the mandrel with his right hand, it fell. As he attempted to catch the mandrel and sleeve, he stumbled and the mandrel struck/pinched his finger on the floor, resulting in a left middle fingertip amputation.

An employee was using a roustabout. As he was lowering the hook for the cable and pulling the slack out of it, the lift began to tip over. The employee went to move out of the way but tripped and fell in the process. The lift then fell on the employee, lacerating his left leg and abdomen.
While rigging down after working for 12 hours, an employee began feeling weak and displaying signs of heat exhaustion. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was using a pressure washer to clean the inside of a fertilizer tank containing ammonium polyphosphate solution when the pressurized steam punctured his left big toe, resulting in infection and hospitalization.
An employee was struck on the lower left leg by two joints of pipe.
An employee was working on the motor of a reclaimer that recycles drilling fluid when they received an electrical shock and burns.

Employees were performing a tubing integrity test. As they were blowing down the pressure from the casing, the nipple assembly came off the casing valve flange onto the ground. The nipple threads and casing valve flange threads failed with the pressure, causing the employees to be pushed to the ground. The injured employee sustained a head injury and was hospitalized.

Employee was working from a ladder with a tool, repairing a conveyor belt system. Weight shifted and the employee tried to regain balance by stepping to the second step. Employee lost footing and fell to the ground, fracturing his femur.

An employee of SM Fencing & Energy Services, Inc. lost his eye sight after receiving a head injury. The employee slipped on the ice at the project site while carrying a railroad tie. After the employee fell to the ground, the railroad tie fell on his head.

On November 16, 2021, a truck driver was removing straps from a load of utility poles on a flatbed trailer. When he removed the last strap, the top pole on the load rolled off and struck the left side of his body, crushing his left wrist and the lower part of his left leg. He was hospitalized, and the leg was medically amputated below the knee. He also suffered a brain injury and two fingers were medically amputated.

An employee was starting to work on the change of a conveyor belt and experienced symptoms of heat exhaustion due to high temperatures. The employee was hospitalized with heat exhaustion and dehydration.
An employee was loading a railcar when a flash fire occurred. The employee sustained first- and second-degree burns to the left side of the body.

An employee was in the mixing room when an asphalt truck arrived to be unloaded. The employee began the procedure for unloading the truck and went outside to the truck to ensure the valve was closed, remove the cap, and attach a hose from the truck to the tanks outside of the mixing room. The cap came off the truck due to pressure behind it and sprayed the employee with the hot asphalt. They sustained burns to the hands, arms, torso, and upper legs.

An employee was part of a crew that was attempting to remove a Christmas tree from a well head when a high-pressure release and blowout occurred. The Christmas tree fell on and broke the employee's leg, requiring hospitalization.
An employee stepped into an uncovered hole and sprained their back.
While working on a natural gas drilling rig, an employee sustained a partial amputation to their little finger.

An employee was setting up five mud tanks and a mud pump. While he was hooking up the fifth mud tank to the fourth mud tank, a gap formed between the hose to the union. He inched the cable over multiple times to close the gap. Then, the driver lifted the mud tank up, which caused the cable line to pull the employee's finger between the truck roller, resulting in an amputation of the end of his left index finger.
An employee was attempting a lift with a crane and caught their left index finger between two shells (36-inch diameter cylinder vessels), resulting in amputation.
An employee suffered heat exhaustion and was given IV fluids. The employee was kept in the hospital for observation.

The injured employee was working on the drill floor assisting to repair the oil well. The employee was using hydraulic-operated tongs when a piece inside the tongs came loose. The employee was fixing it when the lever that powers the tool was hit and the hydraulic tongs crushed his left ring finger, resulting in an amputation above the second joint.

An employee was driving an ATV when it ran over a fallen tree branch. The branch popped up and went through the ATV's floor, striking the employee. The employee suffered a broken arm, a bleeding spleen and liver, and a head laceration.

An employee was welding two sections of pipe on top of a skid platform. The skid platform (2 feet high) collapsed, and the pipe rolled onto the employee's lower leg, fracturing the right ankle. The employee was hospitalized overnight.
An employee was replacing a drill rig's transfer case. The case shifted and amputated the tip of the employee's right index finger.

An employee was exiting a rock crusher and getting onto a 6-foot step ladder. He was holding onto the handrail while getting his feet onto the ladder. His feet were on the second rung from the top when the ladder kicked out from underneath him. He held onto the handrail momentarily and then fell 4 to 5 feet to the ground (gravel pad), breaking his left wrist and suffering a small compression fracture in his lower back. He was hospitalized.
An employee fell off a fixed ladder platform through an open gate, landing about 15-16 feet below. He struck his head, suffered a knee injury, and was hospitalized.
An employee had been operating a pumping unit at a salt water disposal facility when a fire/explosion occurred. The employee sustained third degree burns to 60 percent of his body.

An employee was adjusting the high/low switch on his truck-mounted welder. He was turning around when he lost his footing because it had just rained and his truck bed was slick. He went to steady himself and reached to grab onto something with his hands. His right hand slid underneath the cowling of his welder and two fingers were severely lacerated by the motor fan blades. He was hospitalized.
As a crane truck was rigging down, an employee's hand was caught between the outrigger and the crane. Three fingers on the employee's right hand were crushed and the employee was hospitalized.

On January 6, 2024, an employee was making a swivel connection involving a winch line. As the joint was being tightened, the threads became sticky. The employee was shaking the winch line to loosen it when the bridle caught on the line and wrapped around his finger. His middle finger was amputated past the fingernail and before the first knuckle.
An employee was standing on the ground observing pole line construction when he began showing signs of heat exhaustion, requiring hospitalization.
On May 2, 2024, an employee was dumping a hopper into a bigger dumpster when his left ring finger got caught by the hopper and was amputated.
An employee was stepping from a ladder to an elevated work platform, when they slipped and fell 22 feet to the ground. The employee sustained a fractured right leg that required hospitalization.
An employee was opening the oil tank hatch when a spark ignited the material inside the tank. The employee sustained burns to the face, back and hands.

During rig down, an employee was attempting to move a hose supported on a spreader bar. The hose came free from the spreader bar and swung into a machine, and the employee's left little finger was caught between the hose and the machine. The distal phalanx of the left pinky finger had to be medically amputated.
An employee slipped and fell while walking on a partially constructed walkway beam. His right leg became wedged and fractured on a support brace during the fall.

An employee climbed a ladder to assess the next level of a metal roof. He stepped on a shingle and fell 8 feet through the roof to the ground, breaking his right index finger, left middle finger, right hip, and back.
An employee was securing a stand of drilling pipe with a chain wrench when the wrench broke and hit his hand, breaking his wrist and finger.

An employee was making rounds to collect readings from petroleum tanks. He followed a pathway that had several ground-level protrusions from decommissioned pipe conduits, electrical grounding, and a support strut. The employee tripped on a conduit stub, lost his balance, and fell, landing on his left hip. He was hospitalized with a broken left hip.

Two employees were working on a perforating gun when it detonated in the shop. One employee suffered burns to the hands and hearing loss. The other employee's left hand was amputated and they sustained burns to the upper torso. Both employees were hospitalized.
An employee was pressure washing pipes when the fitting on the spray wand broke and the hot water contacted the employee, resulting in burns to his stomach and thighs.

An employee delivering and removing skids was injured while unloading 12-inch clamps from the flatbed of the truck. The clamps got caught on the employee's clothing and pulled him off of the truck, injuring his lower back.

An employee was performing a hot tap. The employee set a completion plug in preparation of removing the completion plug stopple tool. The tool was not completely set, and gas pressure and metal debris were released from the blow out. The employee sustained multiple contusions and abrasions to the chest, neck and face area, loss of eyes, and finger amputations.

An employee was transferring water at high pressure through a hose. The hose failed and a jet of water knocked the employee through the air approximately 150 feet. When the employee landed on the ground he suffered a shoulder injury.
An employee welding a cable guide pipe to a tank containing road tar suffered burns to his right side legs, arm, neck, and face when the contents of the tank caught on fire.

A crew of five employees used two forklifts along with a telehandler to load and carry pipe that had been cut into 125-foot sections from the fuel pier to the parking lot for painting. The injured employee was guiding the pipe while it was being moved by the forklift. The pipe struck a bush and began swaying and the injured employee's hand was caught between the pipe and the building next to it. The employee's right ring and pinky fingers were amputated.
An employee was welding pipes when his left index and middle finger were caught and amputated in a pipe clamp.
Two employees were fusing two sections of polyline. When the fusing device was activated, the area became engulfed in flames. Both employees were hospitalized with burns to the face and hands.
Pipeline was being cleaned using a pig. The pig shot out of the pipeline and struck the employee, causing injuries to the lower part of his body.
A maintenance employee slipped on ice while applying salt to ice on the ground in the fenced-in yard of the facility. He slipped and broke his left fibula and dislocated his left ankle.
An employee was replacing a natural gas pipeline when he slipped on ice and fractured his left ankle.
An employee was performing well test operations and experienced heat exhaustion. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was on a scaffold while painting a ceiling when he fell off the scaffold to the floor, resulting in a fractured right wrist and an injured left brow.

An employee was welding on the access door to a 21,000 gallon tank containing an asphalt product identified as AC. A flame was observed, by the spotter, moments before a blast. The welder was blown into the air and landed on the platform. The welder sustained burns and was hospitalized.

An employee was opening the top steam vent on the main fractionator. The trapped hot condensate from the vent leaked out and landed on the employee's back and shoulders. The employee was hospitalized with second degree burns.

An employee finished rigging and was walking in an area where a crew was loading an exchanger bundle on a trailer when the load shifted, pinning the employee between the active load and an adjacent stationary load. The employee suffered a fractured left femur and pelvis.

Two employees were looking for steel tubing in the yard. Employee 1 knelt down to read the size numbers on the tubing. Employee 2 pulled out a piece of tubing and then tripped over a white mesh bag of parts from a delivery. The tubing was dropped on employee 1's right middle finger, amputating the fingertip.
An employee was using a sandblasting gun on a pipeline. The gun hit his right arm and the sandblast media caused an open wound on the forearm.

Two employees were unloading and loading propane cylinders. A leaking propane tank was placed in front of a makeshift structure. Propane gas accumulated within the structure and an explosion occurred. Both employees suffered second and third degree burns that required hospitalization.
An employee was cleaning a tank of sand using a high-pressure water hose. The high-pressure water ran across his right foot and cut the big toe.
An employee was bitten on the wrist by an insect. He went into anaphylactic shock later that day and collapsed. He was hospitalized.
An employee was lighting a cutting torch to remove an out-of-service tank when a second tank ignited. The employee suffered a broken leg and second degree burns to the face.

An employee was removing a thread protector off the end of an alloy when the alloy shifted and pinched their finger between it and the catwalk. The employee sustained an open fracture of the left index finger and a fingertip amputation.
An employee was loading a dozer into a trailer when he fell off the dozer onto the trailer platform and then onto the ground, resulting in a laceration to his left elbow.
An employee was using a cutting torch to heat up bolts that had seized up. The bolts caught on fire in a flash burn, and the employee suffered burns to the arms and elbows.
An employee received flash fire burns while working on a non-functioning vaporizer at the 13-mile, full-service terminal vicinity in Williston, North Dakota.
An employee was about to flip a breaker when he suffered a burn to his right hand.

An employee was transferring product from a top tote tank to the bottom tote tank when the leg of the top tote tank shifted causing the top tote tank to pinch the employee's right thumb between the top tote tank and the bottom tote tank spark arrestor. The employee suffered a partial amputation to his right thumb.
An employee was picking up a bushing when it amputated the tip of his middle finger.
An employee was latching a gooseneck trailer onto a truck. His left hand was caught at the point of attachment, and he suffered a partial amputation to the finger at the first knuckle.

An employee was performing abrasive blasting on two six-inch pipes. While rolling the pipe in the kneeling position, the blast nozzle engaged. They sustained an abrasion of the right inner thigh from the abrasive blasting media contacting them at 95 PSI.
An employee was loading glycerol byproduct into a trailer. A plunger valve slipped out of his hand, lacerating his right ring finger and amputating the fingertip.

An employee was performing maintenance on a load cell. Their right hand was on an RPM sensor of rotating weights when the pump jack cycled on, resulting in amputation of three fingertips on the employee's right hand.
An employee's left little finger was pinched between a wrench and a forklift bucket, resulting in an amputation.
An employee was positioning a pipe for welding when his left middle finger got pinched between the pipe and a spacer, resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee was operating a service rig with a snubbing crew when a flash fire or explosion occurred and severely burned the employee.
An employee was walking around equipment, tripped over hydraulic lines and fell to the ground. The employee sustained a broken hip.

A crew was dismantling a rig. They were closing the split spider after removing it from the casing when the injured employee's left hand was caught between the split spider and the rig's master bushing, which was also on the rig's floor. The employee suffered a laceration to the middle finger and fractures to the middle and ring fingers.
The employee was walking, tripped over a wooden pallet, and fell breaking his hip.
