An employee was climbing up a rough-terrain crane. He hit his hard hat on the jib above him, lost his balance, and fell to the crane deck and then to the ground about 4.5 feet below the deck. He suffered rib fractures.
An employee had finished two coke oven charges and was hospitalized for heat exhaustion after his shift.
An employee fell from the top of a trailer loaded with bundles of tubes. He landed on the concrete walking surface 61 inches below, breaking two ribs and suffering shoulder, back, and lung injuries.
An employee was power washing the shop when he was struck by a reversing forklift that ran over and broke his right leg.

An employee was repairing an artificial lift. The employee opened a valve on the lift that caused a rapid release of energy, and the employee was struck by an object. The employee suffered fractures to the skull, right orbital socket, and right cheek. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was walking into the dog house to warm up and closed the door on her hand resulting in a fractured right thumb.

The employee was welding from a spider lift. While moving the spider lift from one location to another, the employee got his hand caught between the handrail and a steel plate resulting in the loss of the left ring fingertip (bone exposed).

An employee was pressure washing a piece of drilling equipment when he slightly slipped, lost his balance, and ran the tip of the pressure washer wand across his foot, causing an injection wound. He was hospitalized with a foot laceration from the high-pressure water.
An employee was near a hybrid separator when it malfunctioned, resulting in a flash fire that burned the employee's upper body.

An employee was delivering lubricant to a customer location. After the employee had pulled a lubricant hose from the tanker and inserted the nozzle into the tank, the employee turned around and tripped over an engine stand, resulting in a fall. The employee's right hip was fractured.
An employee was rigging down a well servicing rig. As the derrick was lowered, it severed his right index finger and thumb under the knuckle. He was hospitalized.
An employee was restarting a vapor combustion unit when a burner lit, causing a flash fire. The employee suffered second degree burns.
An employee fell from a flatbed trailer to the ground while securing a load. He landed on his right leg and injured his pelvis.
An employee was inspecting a pipeline after hydroblasting. The employee was blasted with a sudden burst of high-pressure steam, suffering burns to the shoulders, hands, and knees.
On June 25, 2018, an employee was using a sling to offload 120-gallon tanks from the back of a truck. He fell from the truck to the ground, sustaining a lumbar compression fracture.

Employee 1 was operating a dozer's winch from inside the cabin. While attempting to unhook from a D-ring, he had to loosen the tension of the cable. Upon doing so, employee 2 walked over to the winch and grabbed the cable with her left hand. When employee 1 moved the controls to spool out the winch, employee 2's left hand was pulled into the cables. Employee 2 sustained a broken left ring finger and a partial amputation to her left little finger.
An employee was removing bolts from a wellhead tree when the tree fell onto his left leg, resulting in lower leg fractures.

An employee was helping to remove sand from holding tanks during hydraulic fracturing treatment rigging breakdown. A pipe containing an auger was being used to remove sand from a tank. There was an opening at the end to allow the sand to drop from the pipe, and the employee thought the pipe was stopped up. While inspecting the opening, the employee's left-hand index finger was amputated to the distal joint and the middle finger was severely lacerated by the rotating auger inside the pipe.
An employee was holding a back-pressure regulator. A pipe came apart (under tension from a forklift) and injured the employee's left hand, lacerating and fracturing the index finger.

On 11/22/2015 at 11:50 a.m. an employee was isolating the gas line to identify the point of a suspected ice plug. He walked over to the meter when the hammer union on a two inch gas line disconnected and the pipe struck his leg injuring the tibia and fibula.
An employee was working on the engine of a compressor when a flash fire occurred, burning the employee's hands and face. He was hospitalized.
On July 3, 2017, an employee was installing PVC pipe and using a chop saw when the employee experienced heat stress and heat exhaustion symptoms. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was running a line moling machine to clean the inside of pipe. When the employee went to pressure up the system using a 20-k water line, water from the hose injected into the pinky finger on his left hand.
An employee was attempting to adjust a glycol wrap on a pipe when it shifted. High-pressure water then exited the pipe and struck the employee, knocking him to the ground and breaking his ulna.

An employee was on the stabbing board to hang the tong line. He unhooked the derrick climber from his harness and when he let go of it he was hit in the mouth, lost his footing, and fell even though his lanyard was attached. His face hit the standpipe of the derrick and the 3 foot fall injured his back.

Employee was working from the derrick monkey board latching and unlatching tubing. As he was unlatching the elevator that has horns and a locking mechanism, the employee's harness got caught on the horns. The horns pulled the harness and pulled him down causing small fractures in his knees that required surgery.

An employee was checking for a seam under a suspended pipe. The sling holding the pipe shifted and the pipe lowered onto his right index finger, crushing the tip. The fingertip was amputated past the nail.
An employee was sprayed with hot water when a nearby bleeder valve was under pressure that caused the valve to release. This resulted in burns to their legs and lower torso.
An employee was rigging some 2-inch manifold piping near a well head when some of the piping tipped and struck the employee's lower left leg, causing a compound fracture.

An employee was ventilating a building containing a gas leak and the gases ignited when the employee opened the door. The employee suffered first degree burns to the face and neck and second degree burns to both hands.

An employee was replacing the well house. After installing the new well house, the employee drilled a 2- to 3-inch hole in the side of the well house to run a 2-inch pipe. The employee inserted the pipe into the hole and secured it inside the well house. The employee then traveled outside the well house to apply tape onto the threaded section of the new pipe. The employee used his left index finger to hold the tape on the threads. The pipe section inside the well house fell from its support and the employee's finger was lacerated, resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee was welding outside when he experienced leg and arm cramps. He was hospitalized due to heat stress and dehydration.
An employee was on the forks of a forklift installing anti-pigeon spikes on the ceiling when his finger was crushed between the forklift and a beam.
An employee suffered a back injury when a hopper that was being lifted by a forklift fell on the employee.

An employee was installing casing joints in a well using tongs when the bite of the tongs malfunctioned and the tongs bucked unexpectedly. The employee's hand got crushed between the tongs and the derrick, causing hand fractures.
While welding a tab to the end of a pipe, an employee was struck in the head by another pipe that was being moved laterally by another employee. The employee suffered an epidural hematoma.
An employee was running a pig through a water line to clear the ice. The pig caused the 12-inch water line to whip and strike the employee, resulting in a head laceration and broken leg.

An employee was walking the floor of a rig when a plug from an assembly on the rig came under pressure and blew off, striking the employee in their left thigh and resulting in an open fracture of the femur.

An employee was cutting the coke or removing the coke from the drum to the loading area. Steam was released during the coke cutting process and the employee suffered burns to the neck/jawline and hand/wrist areas.

An employee was delivering a load to a customer location. As the employee made a right-hand turn onto a road, the tractor trailer tracked off the roadway and overturned. The employee sustained bleeding on the brain, a fractured collarbone, and a fractured finger.

A crew was pulling pipe out of the hole and laying pipe/joint one at a time. The injured employee was laying down a drill collar after removing it when the collar swung and pinched their left little finger against a stationary part. The finger was amputated at the first joint.

An employee was working in front of the side boom when the employee tripped and fell. The side boom moved forward several feet, and the boom track ran over the employee, fracturing their right leg and foot.

An employee was standing on the side of a skid plate while waiting for a welding box to be delivered. A second employee was driving a golf cart to bring the first employee the welding box. The welding box fell onto the accelerator pedal while the driver was approaching the first employee. The golf cart then struck the first employee on the back of his right leg and pushed him onto the skid plate. He sustained a fractured leg.
An employee was performing maintenance on a heater treater. When he opened the heater treater door an explosion occurred. The employee sustained hand, body, and face burns.

An employee was painting pipeline risers. After he completed painting, the employee was cleaning the paint sprayer nozzle with mineral spirits (petroleum base solvent used as paint thinner) when his right hand slipped, causing cleaning solvent to inject into the lower front portion of his left middle finger. The employee was hospitalized and had surgery.
An employee stepped into an area where hot condensate was present and sustained a condensate burn to the lower right leg.

An employee removed the spark plugs and was rotating an engine to evacuate condensate from the cylinders. An unknown source ignited the condensate and natural gas. The employee sustained burns to the back of his hands and upper leg area.

An employee was using a pressure washer at an oil and gas site. The water pressure was approximately 1400 psi. He lost control of the hose and the wand struck the employee's left hand causing a laceration between the thumb and wrist. The employee was hospitalized overnight.
A maintenance employee was attempting to repair/replace an inoperative breaker to a hot oil furnace when an electrical arc flash occurred, causing first degree burns to the employee's hands.

On July 26, 2021, an employee was hydroblasting using a 5,500 psi water blast gun with a 66-inch barrel. The barrel was run across the top of his left boot, lacerating the top of the foot. He was hospitalized, requiring cleaning and stitches for the wound.

An employee was at the top of a fixed ladder mounted on the interior of a 10-foot deep trench box. It was raining and the employee's feet and the ladder were wet. The employee slipped off the ladder and fell onto his back on the plywood flooring of the excavation, sustaining a back injury.
On October 15, 2019, an employee was attempting to secure a barge when his right hand was crushed and lacerated by the winch wheel.

An employee was standing on the floor of a drilling rig while hooking up a Kelly hose to a pipe. The hose struck him below the left shoulder blade, and he rolled off the rig and fell to the ground. He suffered kidney trauma, broken ribs, and a liver laceration.

An employee was preparing to load asphalt into a truck. The employee was about to line up the hose into the opening of the truck when the asphalt in the tanker flashed causing second degree burns to the employee's face and arms.
An employee was exposed to hydrogen sulfide while loading crude oil. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was handing a hot welding torch to his employer when the welding tip touched the employee's left hand between the knuckle and wrist. The employee sustained a burn to the hand.

An employee was cutting a fallen tree that was laying on a telephone cable. When the tree was cut, pressure was released on the telephone cable, which sprung back up and threw the limb toward the employee. He suffered a contusion to the right side of his face.
An employee was pressure washing a gas compression unit when they stepped off a 3-foot high skid and fell to the ground, sustaining an ankle fracture.

A foreman and his crew were about to take a section of a crane hook and move it into position. The foreman stopped work, noticing something wrong, and the pipe shifted and struck his hands while they were on the handrail. He suffered amputation injuries to his left ring and little fingers.

An employee was signaling a forklift operator as a 20-foot-long, 4-inch-thick section of steel pipe was lowered. The pipe came loose and fell striking the employee's head and shoulder. The employee sustained a head laceration and fractured ribs.

An employee was driving a side-boom operator across a temporary bridge. The bridge collapsed and the machine rolled slightly and came to rest at about a 45 degree angle. As the employee disconnected his seat belt, he fell from the machine and landed in the creek bed on his back. The fall caused hairline fractures to his scapula and a rib.
An employee was removing a transducer when high pressure fluid struck his hand, penetrating his skin.

An employee was using a rake to grade hot asphalt in a parking lot. The employee tripped over a car stop and fell onto the hot asphalt, suffering second- and third-degree burns to the lower back and arm. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was lifting a 100-pound exhaust manifold off an engine using a service truck crane. While he was maneuvering the manifold toward the bed of his truck, it struck his left index finger and caught it against a pressure relief valve. He suffered a laceration and fracture to the finger and was hospitalized.

An employee was operating a blender. Noticing that a booster pump was running, he began walking toward it to turn it off. The booster pump deadheaded, causing pressure and steam to build up in the line, and as the employee approached an 8-inch suction hose broke loose from the pump and struck him in the lower left leg. He suffered a compound fracture to the left leg and second-degree steam burns to the torso.
An employee was offloading hydrochloric acid (15% concentration) when the employee was sprayed in the face, suffering acid burns to the face and eyes.

An employee was climbing down a ladder on a tanker truck. The pneumatic guardrail system on the top of the truck retracted and struck the employee. The employee fell to the ground, suffering broken bones.
An employee slipped and twisted his right ankle while attempting to carry a 50-pound bag of seed, fracturing his fibula and tibia.

During the breaking of a connection, an employee was holding a "mud bucket" against a pipe to minimize the splashing of mud on an oil rig floor. As the two pieces of pipe were moved apart, a spray of mud caused the employee to fall and hit his head on a piece of equipment behind him. He suffered a scalp laceration and a skull fracture.

An employee was trying to restart an engine on a compressor that went down. The engine flywheel and starter were not aligned. The employee attempted to use a bar to roll over the flywheel when built-up air pressure caused the entire engine to roll over. The bar then slammed into the employee's left arm, resulting in an injury.
An employee was climbing a fixed ladder. The employee fell about 9 feet to the concrete floor and suffered a right hip fracture and right leg fractures.

An employee was working at a treatment facility construction site. A flatbed had transported a single platform about 1 mile to the site. The platform was strapped onto the flatbed and had wood blocks to keep it from moving. During the transport, one of the pieces of wood vibrated out of position. When the employee released the ratcheted straps, the tubular steel frame platform toppled over and off the flatbed. The platform struck and broke his left leg. He was hospitalized and had surgery.
An employee was operating a vacuum truck when the hose became disconnected and began spraying hot fluid. A fire and then explosion occurred, and the employee suffered serious burns.

An employee was filling a 150-gallon water tank on a drilling rig truck. The pressure of the hose at the water station threw the employee from the platform to the ground 4.5 feet below. The employee suffered broken ribs and a head injury and was hospitalized.
During the filming of a television scene, an employee tripped on the electrical cord for a Christmas tree. She fell to the floor and suffered a broken left hip.
An employee slipped on ice/snow and broke his ankle.
An employee was performing tank gauging on a produced water tank. After opening the tank's thief hatch, the employee was exposed to hydrogen sulfide, suffering headaches and nausea.

An employee was grinding on a structural handrail for a work platform with a grating floor. The employee lost control of the grinder, which lacerated and fractured his left index finger. His left index fingertip was surgically amputated.
An employee slipped on water droplets on the floor and fell, breaking her left hip and right ankle.
On or before February 19, 2015, an employee slipped and fell on ice while carrying a 2-inch x 30-foot-long piece of pipe, resulting in a tibia/fibula fracture to the right leg.

An employee was helping to sandblast an underground pipe with a hose and sandblasting wand when the wand pointed at his arm and released sandblasting material under high pressure. He suffered a serious arm abrasion.
An employee was hospitalized due to heat exhaustion.

Two employees were working on an empty above-ground 2,500-barrel crude oil tank. Employee 1 was welding while employee 2 was watching. Employee 1 saw fire behind the welding smoke and notified employee 2. Before they could get off the tank, they both fell in the tank and sustained burns from the fire.

An employee was standing on the wheel well of a sweeper vehicle. He was checking the radiator water level immediately after shutting the machine down. As he was filling the radiator with water, it began to bubble up, so he dismounted the machine. He landed oddly on the ground and fractured his left leg above the ankle.

A crane was removing a heater from a platform. The heater was lifted up to tighten the chains before resuming the lift, but the heater stack (7 ft. pipe) broke off of the heater. The broken piece struck an employee, who suffered a severe concussion and broken bones in the neck.
An employee was transferring an oil/gas scrubber into a scrap bin. The employee's arm was caught and broken between the scrubber and the wall of the bin.

Employees were working at a steam/hot water-filled drain box and had removed the cover for the drain box. An employee was walking into the area to hook up a vacuum truck when he stepped into the uncovered drain box. He suffered burns to both lower legs, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was participating in work over rig operations. As they were tying ahead, they were caught in the spool and sustained fractures of the tibia, fibula, scapula, and pelvis.
An employee was struck in the shoulder by a casing pipe during a well completion operation. The employee then suffered a reaction to painkillers.
An employee was assisting with moving a length of pipe. The employee tripped and was run over by an excavator resulting in fractures to the lower body.

On September 9, 2020, an employee was attempting to start a vibrating tamper in order to continue compacting backfill material in a completed excavation. The employee pulled the starter cord multiple times. After the pull which started the engine, the pull cord of the vibrating tamper did not recoil correctly. The employee gathered the excess cord in his left hand in order to prevent an additional slip, trip, or fall hazard. When he engaged the throttle of the machine with his right hand, the pull cord retracted, wrapped around the employee s left thumb, and caused a partial amputation of the thumb tip.
An employee was attempting to free a hydraulic line. When the coil tubing was freed it struck the employee in the head causing a skull fracture and a laceration that required stitches.

An employee had unloaded a tracked drill rig off of a trailer and started to drill when the employee's pant leg became caught in the drill auger. As a result, the employee suffered a fracture to the left fibula with contusions and a hematoma, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was in the office shutting down for the day. The employee impacted the back of their head on an unknown object and was hospitalized with a head injury.

A crew had put their tools down after pressure-washing the outsides of two oil tanks. As they walked away, one of the tanks exploded. One of the employees suffered second- and third-degree burns on the back, from the waist up.

An employee was standing within proximity of the drilling pipes as the pipes were being tightened with a wrench and the bucket of a mini excavator. The wrench that was held in place by the excavator bucket slipped, causing the drill pipe to move uncontrollably and strike the employee in the head. The employee sustained a concussion and a cut/laceration.

An employee was attempting to tack weld and repair a tubular steel livestock gate. The gate was in a bind due to a broken component and was positioned in such a way that a gap was present between the broken component and anchoring rail. As the employee placed the left hand on the anchoring rail, it dropped, pinching the soft tissue of the employee's left index finger between the component and anchor. As the employee pulled the hand back, the employee's left index finger was amputated (without bone loss).
An employee's hand was on a cable that was being used to lift a pipe from a rig when his finger was amputated.

At 1:24 p.m. on January 11, 2021, an employee was assisting with curbside Christmas tree pickup when he slipped on ice and fell backward, striking the back of his head on the side of the truck and then on the ground. The employee suffered a left parietal non-displaced skull fracture.

An employee was pushing back a stand of drill pipe on a rig floor. He slipped and fell forward, putting his hands out in front of him to brace his fall. The drill pipe moved back slightly and pinched his right index and middle fingers against the rig floor, resulting in the amputation of the two fingertips above the first knuckle.
An employee was inside a manhole when a 2x4 fell into the hole and hit the top of his finger that was grasping the ladder amputating it.
Employee slipped on ice and broke femur while working on well site in the vicinity of the Anderson 1-4-H location near Williston, North Dakota.
An employee was loading out components of a stacked drilling rig when a beam flipped over and struck the employee. The employee suffered a broken leg and fractured ribs.

Two employees were in a trailer. A lit cigarette ignited gas that had leaked from a propane tank in the trailer, causing an explosion. Both employees suffered second-and third- degree burns to the hands, arms, and face.

An employee was walking along a narrow rural roadway toward the back of a digger derrick truck as another digger derrick truck was moving forward from the opposite direction, passing the parked vehicle. The employee's foot was run over by the tire of the vehicle. The employee sustained fractures to the top of the right foot and a dislocated big toe.

An employee was servicing an oil rig when a rod transfer became hung up, came loose, and struck the employee, knocking him out of a rod basket. He landed face first on a tubing board and broke his leg, jaw, nose, and other facial bones.

An employee was injured and hospitalized after stepping into a containment dike sump area. The containment area is approximately 18 inches deep and is siphoned out of the sump with a steam siphon. At the time of the incident, the siphon was plugged in, which resulted in steam being diverted back into the sump and the water being heated. The employee was burned from about his left knee to his left foot.
While stepping onto an assembly, an employee tripped on the edge and fell forward. The employee's jaw struck an angle iron and broke in three places.

An employee was on top of the tanker truck loading fuel into the tanker. The vapors ignited causing an explosion and throwing the employee 20 feet into the air. The employee suffered third degree burns, broken bones and internal bleeding.

While climbing a ladder to an acid gas/ammonia gas drum platform, an employee missed the second rung from the top of the ladder and fell approximately 7 feet. The employee suffered a fractured hip and lacerated elbow.

An employee arrived at a location to shut some production wells. While walking through the location, the employee tripped on a 1-inch piece of pipe and fell to the ground on their right side. The employee sustained a fractured hip requiring hospitalization.
An employee was replacing catalyst parts in the heat and became ill due to heat exhaustion, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was working outside on July 17, 2018, preparing for the next day's job when he started not feeling well. The next day, July 18, 2018, the employee was at a customer location working and started vomiting and was unable to keep any fluids down. The employee was hospitalized for heat exhaustion and renal failure.
An employee was vacuuming catalyst inside a confined space. A piece of the catalyst rolled down from the pile and struck his leg, breaking the femur. He was hospitalized.
An employee was attaching a compressor to a skid with a pneumatic impact driver. The employee's finger got caught in the driver, which tore off his fingertip; the injury did not involve the bone.
An employee was flushing out the coil tubing due to a frozen line. He started hammering on the line and it broke apart. He was struck in the chest by the high pressure hose.

An employee was tasked with offloading a marine vessel. He was resetting the loading arm back into place when his left hand was caught between the load arm head and a fixed dock component, amputating his index and middle fingertips.

An employee was on a landing above a frac tank. The employee put a strap stick into the tank; when it hit the bottom of the tank, the fluids in the tank ignited. The flash fire caused the employee to jump or fall, and he suffered two broken legs as well as burns to the arm.

Employee was changing out a piece of pipe while installing underground conduits on a directional drilling rig. He was struck by a wrench. The employee was taken to the hospital with injuries to his forearm.
Two employees were removing ball valves. When the employees began to install the gaskets, a flash fire occurred. One employee suffered burns to the face.

An employee was dismantling a lubricant barrel with a torch when it exploded. The explosive force blew out the bottom of the drum, which flew up and struck the employee's face, smashing the welding helmet he was wearing, sending him backwards, and causing him to hit his head on the concrete floor. He suffered facial lacerations, a skull fracture, and bleeding on the brain.

Employees were installing grating that consisted of 4 sheets (approximately 4 feet by 5 feet), cumulatively weighing approximately 800 pounds. When the employees disconnected the load from the crane, they realized the corner of the grating rested on the edge of an existing guard rail toe plate. The injured employee attempted to lift the grating upwards while his coworker used a spud wrench to shift the grating off the toe plate. The grating shifted and caught the injured employee's left index finger between the grating and structural steel. He suffered an avulsion to his left index finger flesh beneath his fingertip, which was crushed and cut. He required surgery and was hospitalized overnight.

An employee was removing a high-density polyethylene (HDPE) flange from a steel host pipe that had an HDPE liner installed. As the liner seal was broken, a puff of gas that was trapped in the annular space between the liner and steel pipe was released and ignited. The fire caused second degree burns to the employee's wrists and face.
Two employees were welding pipe when the 9x9 steel welding hut blew over due to a microburst. One employee was hospitalized for a fractured leg and hip.

At a remote location, the injured employee was running a pig through the pipeline when the pig became stuck. As the employee was venting gas to the atmosphere to free the pig, a spark ignited the gas vapors, causing the employee to sustain second-degree burns to their face and left elbow.

Two employees were setting a steel beam that was attached to the choker of a crane. The crane operator picked up the beam and started cabling up. As the beam started rising, it became caught on part of the structure. The crane continued to pull up. The beam broke loose from the structure that it was caught on and swung free, striking the two employees. One of the employees was hospitalized with fractured ribs, pulmonary contusions, and a collapsed lung.
An employee was helping re-spool the winch line on a tubing tester truck when the line caught his right hand. Four fingers were amputated.

Employee 1 was setting up his survey instrument at the edge of a concrete apron surrounding an 11-foot-deep concrete utility vault with a 9x9 steel access cover/lid. Employee 2, then walked behind employee 1, stepping onto the steel vault access cover/lid. The cover gave way, causing employee 2 and the steel vault cover to fall into the vault approximately 11 feet below. Employee 1 fell 8 feet, striking an existing pipeline valve located within the vault. Employee 2 was hospitalized for fractures to the ribs on the left side. Employee 1 did not require hospitalization.
An employee was working outdoors and became ill due to heat exhaustion.
An employee was walking toward equipment when the employee tripped on a 2-inch pipe on the ground. The employee hit their nose and upper lip and suffered a dislocated shoulder.

While an employee was using a manual post driver, his left middle finger was trapped between the driver and a post. The fingertip was crushed; he was hospitalized, and the tip was medically amputated.

The rig crew was topping off the well with fluid when the operator noticed that the gauge was reading 0 psi. The rig operator leaned over the well head to check for flow inside the well head when an ice plug that had formed released from the well head and struck the employee in the face. The employee suffered injuries to his face and eyes.

At about 11:20 a.m. on March 14, 2019, a truck driver was working on top of a tractor trailer to check the fuel level. A gust of wind blew the employee off the top of the trailer. The employee suffered broken bones and was hospitalized.
An employee was performing gas service work outdoors in extreme heat when they became ill. The employee was hospitalized with dehydration.
An employee was hospitalized for complications due to a muscle injury after working on the battery.

Employees were rigging down and started removing fluid from a line. They placed a clamp at one end of the line, but the clamp loosened and two employees were struck. One employee was hospitalized with internal injuries.

Three employees were cleaning a heater treater when a gas build-up caused an explosion in the building. Two of the employees received minor injuries; the third was hospitalized, having suffered a severe laceration across the forehead, burns to the face and neck, and a fractured spine.

An employee was installing light posts when the derrick truck swung the light post and contacted the power line behind them. The trailer holding the post became energized, and the employee received severe electrical burns.

An employee was repairing a cooling fan and replacing the fan belt. The employee was using a screw driver to put the belt on when it slipped, catching the employee's finger between the pulley and fan belt. The employee's left fingertip was amputated.
An employee was moving a panel switch to the open position on a 480-volt motor control center breaker when an electrical arc flash occurred, burning the employee's eyes, face, neck, and hands.
An employee was offloading iron from a trailer when the employee's right index finger got caught between a 4-inch iron, which fell from above, and the edge of the trailer.

The governor on a portable welder had been replaced. While an employee was checking the wiring behind the governor, a coolant fan blade broke his left index finger and caused tendon damage and lacerations on the other fingers.
An employee got caught between a trailer and truck while directing the truck driver to back up. The employee's leg was crushed, and the employee was hospitalized.
An employee suffered an electric shock and/or burns on the hands and fingers while installing distribution lines.

The injured employee was inserting the nozzle of a tubing tester into the testing bars when the tubing tester lowered the bars. The injured employee's finger was crushed between the nozzle and the wiper plate, resulting in amputation of the distal right index fingertip.
An employee was welding on a mud pump when an explosion occurred. A pipe cap blew off and hit his stomach, injuring his spleen.

An employee was a spotter for a forklift operator. He was walking backwards when he stumbled and fell to the ground. The forklift driver stopped and the load (pit liner material roll) rolled off the forks, striking the employee and breaking his legs.
An employee was flagging trucks into a job site when a pickup truck drove through the construction zone and struck the employee, who suffered two broken ribs and a bruised elbow.
An employee was walking across a concrete parking lot when they slipped and fell on a patch of ice, resulting in a fractured leg.
An employee was opening a high-pressure relief valve with a pressure bar. He was pulling down on the bar when it gave way, causing him to fall on the second bar. He tore his left triceps and bicep.

On June 5, 2017, an employee was rebuilding a bench cylinder when pressure began building in the cylinder and released. The cylinder then struck the employee in the abdomen and pushed the employee into a locker. The employee suffered internal bleeding and crushing injuries, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was preparing a pump for maintenance. When the employee removed a cover, chemicals were released into the air. The employee was exposed to hydrogen sulfide and methyl mercaptan and was hospitalized.
An employee was attaching a tong to a pipe when his left leg was caught in the tong pull line and the drill string, resulting in a left leg amputation.
An employee was checking around a work area. The employee tripped on a ground rod that was sticking up about 2 inches from the ground and suffered a broken left knee.
Employees were engaging in horseplay when the injured employee lost his balance and fell from the back of a digger derrick truck to the ground. The employee's leg was fractured in two places.

An employee was cleaning a sight glass on a gas separation machine that was located on top of a self contained/self evacuating tank. When the valve that connected the well bore to the gas separation machine was opened, gas/vapor ignited, causing a flash fire that burned the employee's face and hands.

An employee was trying to lower the level on a condensate boiler by opening a pump case drain line. The plugged condensate line shifted unexpectedly and pinched the employee's left hand against a stanchion. The employee suffered burns to the hand.

A drill collar was being lowered from a higher elevation pad next to the location where the rig was located. An employee placed a board as a chock under the drill collar. As the forklift forks were being removed from under the collar, the collar started to roll. The drill collar caught the right edge of the employee's boot and began to pull his leg under the collar. The employee sustained compound fractures to both bones in his lower right leg.

An employee was lowering the boom of the manlift. The manlift basket became entangled with a rope attached to a pulley used to hoist screens and tools to the top of the plant. As the manlift descended it put tension on the rope which broke the gantry frame. A section of the frame struck the employee's head/shoulder area. The employee lost consciousness and sustained multiple fractures to his skull, face, shoulder and ribs. The employee was wearing personal protective equipment at the time.

Three employees were assembling a mast for a mobile rig derrick. Each of the two sections are approximately 60 feet long. The lower mast was positioned on stands. The upper mast was supported by an overhead crane. The injured employee was standing at the base on the lower mast behind the winch skid. He was using a crane and a winch that is mounted on a forklift skid to slide the top mast into the lower mast. The upper section of the mast became misaligned and the force from the crane and winch operations caused the mast to shift 4 feet. This caused the winch skid to shift 4 feet back as well, pinning the employee's left foot between the base of the winch and the base of the forklift mast. The employee sustained two fractures in his foot.

Employees had finished clearing trees for a pipeline and were walking back to the trucks. The injured employee slipped and fell to the ground after stepping on a rock covered with leaves. The employee suffered a broken leg and was hospitalized.

An employee was adjusting the operator console to raise it to a higher level. He removed the bracket that connects the console to the rail system so he could begin raising it. The console shifted, causing the employee to fall 10 feet, resulting in a shoulder fracture and head laceration.

An employee was opening a hatch on a bulk cement truck when pressure inside of the truck caused the hatch cover to slide off and up, striking the employee. The employee sustained a non-displaced pelvis fracture, a right linear temporal fracture and a subdural hematoma.

An employee was removing a clamp from the electrical submersible pump string of a laydown machine when their left index finger was caught between the clamp and the machine. The employee sustained a partial amputation between the first knuckle and the fingernail.
An employee was using a chain to winch an object when the chain snapped and a tow cable smashed through the window and broke the employee's right arm.

An employee was assisting a customer to position a shaker basket on a shaker skid utilizing a forklift operated by the customer. Three of the employee's fingers on the left hand were caught and injured between the shaker basket and the cross support of the shaker skid.

A truck driver along with another employee had just finished draining a tanker. They were unhooking the hose from the tanker when hot liquid asphalt struck the driver's arm causing severe burns. The driver was hospitalized.
An employee was overcome by heat stress while conducting oil-well servicing operations.

An employee was rebuilding a setting tool, attempting to seat the lower cylinder onto the cylinder head by tapping the setting tool onto the trailer floor. As the employee pushed down on the setting tool, the mandrel stroked in the setting sleeve and pinched and amputated their right middle finger.

A crew was rigging down when a winch line became hung up on the operations platform. The platform then failed and an employee was caught between the rails and control panel, suffering bodily contusions.
A pressure gauge was removed while observing a pressure survey on the crude unit and an employee received first and second degree burns.
An employee was standing on the rig, spooling the line, when the tubing line got caught around both ankles. The unit engaged and he sustained a left ankle fracture and right ankle sprain.

Employees were filling 55-gallon drums of finished lubricant from a cook kettle. The injured employee was operating the kettle valve when the seal on the filter basket failed under pressure, spraying the employee with 300-400-degree F lubricant. The employee sustained second-and third-degree burns to 20% of the body, including his chest, arms, and legs and was hospitalized.
An employee was troubleshooting the dehydration unit at the compressor station when he sustained burns to the hand and face from a fire. He was hospitalized.

An employee was aligning/guiding a workover rig onto a well-head using a spacing cable when his left ring finger was caught between the spacing cable and the rod blowout preventer, resulting in a fingertip amputation.

An employee was using a high-pressure hose to wash a tank. The valve at the end of the hose broke due to the pressure, causing the hose to then strike the employee in the throat. The employee sustained severe injuries to the pharynx and neck.

An employee was using a motorized saw to cut the top off a test barrel. His left glove got caught and pulled into the saw, resulting in amputation of the index fingertip. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was detaching a 200-pound bale at or near an oil well site. He tripped on a rock and fell backward and the bale fell on his abdomen, causing internal bleeding.

An employee was replacing a seized gearbox on an oil well using a breaker bar. After the breaker bar broke the gearbox loose, the bar struck the employee in the face, causing a fractured nasal bone and a laceration from the crown of the nose to above the right eye. The employee was hospitalized.

Employees were installing an inline pole to increase the ground clearance of a sagging power line. Once the new pole was in place, the employee in the bucket truck attached the energized line to the jib on the new pole. As the employees finished emplacing the new pole, the energized line (7,620 volts) broke loose from the jib on the new pole. Due to the sag in the energized wire, it dropped low enough to contact the boom of the digger derrick truck. Two employees standing next to the truck sustained an electrical shock.

An employee was installing an outrigger on a frac unit. The employee climbed a ladder to install the top pivot pin while a loader was positioning the outrigger. The top pin would not fully slide into place because the bottom pin's eye was not aligned properly. The employee dismounted the ladder and pushed the lower part of the outrigger to align the pins and eyes with the mount. When the employee placed the lower pin into the eyes, the top pin fell through the eyes and struck the employee's right hand, smashing the index and middle fingers.

An employee was cutting welding wire from a welding machine's welding head when he was struck from behind by the welding machine boom and knocked into a steel pipe that was being loaded onto the welding rack. He suffered a ruptured intestine and torn ligament in the right leg.

An employee was preparing an oven for charging and cracked the seal of the jump lid to release pressure. Flames unexpectedly released from the oven and burned the employee's right ring and little fingers. The employee sustained second-degree burns.

An employee was installing a pump during the fracking process when he felt lightheaded and began vomiting. He started having heat cramps and was hospitalized after suffering severe dehydration while operating equipment outside with temperatures of 105F.
An employee was found unresponsive inside of a trailer with a running generator. He was hospitalized for carbon monoxide exposure.
An employee was pressure washing a roll-off box when the employee contacted the pressurized water, suffering a left foot injury.

Two electricians were troubleshooting an HVAC (condenser) unit in a control room. Both employees went to the control room and applied group lockout to a single disconnect rated at 250 VDC power. After locking out the power to the control room and condenser unit, the employees began troubleshooting several deficiencies they observed while looking through the control panel. After repairing those items, the two employees removed the locks and validated that the repairs were working. The employees observed everything working as required except the HVAC compressor. The injured employee went up to the condenser area on an elevated walking surface that was covered in blaze which is a byproduct of the coke produced at the plant. The accumulation of blaze created an uneven surface. The employee had to remove an exterior covering or guard to validate that 250 VDC was coming from the thermostat to the junction box on the compressor motor. The employee squatted down and lost his balance before checking for 250 VDC. The employee reached to catch himself and in doing so grabbed the belts that drive the compressor motor. When contact was made, the motor began running and the employee's left hand was pulled through the pulleys amputating his left middle and ring fingers.
An employee was working on trucks when his shop rag ignited from a spark, causing his clothing to catch on fire. He sustained burns on his arms and legs and was hospitalized.

On September 14, 2015, at approximately 10:30am, a worker suffered an amputation of the left pinky finger just above the palm while unloading pipe from a pipe trailer. The employee was standing towards the tractor side of the trailer and a side boom with sling was unloading the pipe. The load was lowered near the tractor in an effort to raise the pipe above the back stanchion on the trailer. As the pipe slowly moved, the load struck a stanchion or DOT fender and the employee's hand was crushed in the load of pipe. No tag line was used.
An employee fell from a tractor and struck her head on the ground, resulting in a concussion. She was hospitalized overnight.
An employee was operating a four-wheeler to take soil samples when it hit a rock. The four-wheeler rolled over onto the employee's left leg fracturing the fibula and tibia.

An employee was collecting a sample at a closed loop station. Recently installed tubing came loose, spraying the employee with spent acid. The employee suffered second-degree burns to the right forearm and left wrist.

An employee was preparing to install pipe into a bore hole when the pipe began bouncing on cribbing. He put his right hand underneath the pipe, and his right pinky fingertip was pinched and amputated between the pipe and the cribbing.
An employee was entering a production line to weld a tab on a pipe when the employee's left leg (between the ankle and knee) was caught and injured between a steel pipe and a roller breaker.

An employee was about to dump sand from a hopper, raised on the forks of a forklift. As the hopper's weight shifted forward and it began to dump, the employee's left middle finger was pinched between the forklift fork and the metal frame of the hopper. The fingertip was crushed, and the employee underwent a medical amputation at the first knuckle.
Two employees were burned when a bubble tower exploded creating a flash fire during maintenance work on a well site.

On April 7, 2022, an employee was conducting a high-pressure wash of a frack tank when oil and gas frack water entered their eyes, resulting in blindness in the right eye. An eyewash station was not available at the time.

An employee was walking by an equipment battery (tank battery) when a leak occurred around a heater that caused a flash fire. He was wearing flame-resistant clothing and sustained burns to his palms and back.
An employee was preparing to work on a flare when it discharged oil. The oil struck the employee, causing burns to the body, wrist, and hand.

An employee was using a spray wand connected to a hot water pressure washer to open up a frozen produce water tank. The produce water vented hydrocarbon vapors near the hot water pressure washer causing a fire. Two employees received second and third degree burns to the face, neck and hands.
An employee was spotting for a backhoe when its track struck the employee. The employee's left leg was amputated from the knee down.

An employee was cleaning a derrick with a power washer. The employee slipped on a wet surface while untangling the power washer hose. As he reached out to catch himself, part of the derrick caught his right little finger and removed the flesh, exposing the bone.
An employee slipped on ice in a gravel parking lot and fell to the ground. The employee suffered a broken right hip.

A Kinder Morgan employee accessed the top of a truck during a loading operation. When he opened the dome lid, alkylate pressure released and propelled him onto the truck rack roof, then to the ground below. He suffered multiple fractures and a torn artery in the skull, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was conducting work on the 60-feet-high platform of an oil derrick, operating rigging to move piping into position. The employee became sick, vomited, experienced cramps, and was eventually hospitalized for heat-related health issues.

An employee was rinsing the inside of a tank with water from a 1-inch hose. The water pressure surged and the hose whipped around. Its metal nozzle struck the employee's head and face, causing a fracture to the right mandible, a head laceration on the right side of the head behind the ear, and trauma to the right side of the head.
An employee was working inside the shop when a propane leak caused an explosion. The employee suffered third degree burns.
Employees were welding and sandblasting a heat treater. A flash fire occurred inside the tank, and an employee suffered burns to the face and a wrist.
An employee was hydrostatic pressure-testing a section of pipeline when a pipe coupling separated and struck him in the face, lacerating his upper lip and causing dental trauma.

An employee was disassembling a one-tier tubular scaffold. The employee removed the cross bracing first. When a coworker removed the planks, the scaffold members came down and struck the employee, causing back and pelvis bruises.
Two employees were installing a protective goal post for overhead power lines when the post made contact with the energized line, causing the employees to receive an electrical shock.
Employee received an electric shock when he placed his wrench near an energized bolt on a conductor he was removing.
An employee stepped out of a pickup truck, which began to move. The employee fell and the truck ran over the employee's right leg, causing tibia and fibula fractures that required surgery.

An employee was pinning tubing together to skid the rig. The employee's hands were placed between the two pieces, and the left pinky and ring fingers got pinched. Both fingers were surgically amputated.
An employee was hoisting a propane tank when the chain rigging caught the employee's hand, resulting in an index finger amputation.

An employee was in a boat, inspecting a pipeline, when the boat hit something in the water and ejected the employee from the seat. The employee hit the boat floor and suffered a forehead laceration and fractured left wrist.

Employees were moving a pipeline inspection tool barrel. The injured employee was pulling on the rigging in order to allow a forklift to move the barrel through an open door. As the barrel was coming through the door, the rigging slipped off the fork and the barrel landed on the employee's foot. The employee's two left toes adjacent to his big toe were amputated.
While walking at grade under an asphalt rail car loading rack, an employee tripped on concrete that was protruding from the walkway. The employee fell and sustained five broken ribs.
An employee was making confined space entries to clean a tank when they began to experience symptoms of heat-related illness, cramps, and heat exhaustion. The employee was hospitalized.

While an employee was moving a small pile of hot material with a bobcat, a flash of steam entered the cab of the bobcat. The employee exited the cab and tripped into a pool of hot water, receiving first and second degree burns and requiring hospitalization.
An employee was guiding a load being lifted by a crane. The employee's right little finger was caught between the crane hook and the load and partially amputated.

A crew was on a drilling floor making a drill pipe connection. One employee was using a 5-foot bar with the pipe tongs, to apply pressure, to make the pipe fitting tight. The bar slipped and struck the employee in the chest, resulting in rib fractures to the right side.

The injured employee was holding tubing while another employee used a sledgehammer to straighten out a bent tube. The roof that was being lifted fell down with the piping and crushed the injured employee's left thumb, resulting in amputation.
An employee was assisting with moving a 12-inch PVC pipe. The pipe shifted, pinching the employee's left index finger against a support post. The employee's finger was fractured.
An employee was unpacking boxes at a receiving table. The employee tripped on a cable that had dropped off the table and fell, suffering a broken hip. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee suffered a hand injury while performing routine maintenance on a pump jack at or near Pierre Creek Nelson 44-23 HR in McKenzie County, North Dakota.

An employee was inspecting noise from a pumping unit. As he went to push on the belt guard, the employee was pinned between the crank arm and the base of the unit, resulting in a lacerated liver, and bruising to the chest, arms, back, and shoulders.
While fueling a truck, an employee observed a pool of liquid, then noticed mist coming from a pipe. The employee developed respiratory symptoms resembling those of ammonia exposure.
An employee was on a 4-foot podium ladder when the wind blew it over. He fell, and his left middle fingertip was amputated.
An employee was applying pipe identification to a pipe moving along a v-roller line. A support frame failed and the pipe fell over, injuring the employee's hips/pelvis and leg.
An employee was repairing a meter run and began to experience cramping. The employee was hospitalized for heat exhaustion.

An employee removed plywood that was covering a hole so that a crane could fly in a flange. The employee fell through the hole in the floor, contacting a flange approximately 41 inches below. The employee then fell approximately 47 inches, contacting an aluminum step stool, before falling approximately 19 inches to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with a spinal injury that required surgery.
An employee was performing maintenance on a forklift when they fell approximately 2 feet off the forklift and landed on a tote, resulting in multiple fractured ribs.

An employee hoisted the lubricator up off a well head using a winch and was inspecting the tool stream. The winch malfunctioned and continued to raise the lubricator up which was 8 feet long. It was raised approximately 15 feet off the ground. The cable snapped and the lubricator fell striking the employee and causing a laceration to his chest approximately 6-8 inches long and 1 1/2 inches deep.
An employee was placing chemical hoses at the top of the tub of a blender. His right ring finger was pinched inside an inlet valve actuator and was amputated to the first joint.

An employee was helping an aerial access driver load multiple mobile light plants that were off-rent onto an aerial access trailer. The employee was bent down in a squat position, attempting to adjust the tongue of a mobile light tower, when the aerial access driver put his back against the rear light plant and shoved it forward. The employee's index finger was caught between the transport trailer deck and tongue of the mobile light tower, amputating the left index fingertip.
An employee was driving downhill to return a UTV (utility terrain vehicle) to a truck when he lost control and capsized, breaking 11 ribs.
An employee was operating a drill press when their glove got caught in the drill, resulting in an amputation of the left pinky finger.
A forklift collision broke an employee's heel and ankle.
A valve cap, under pressure, struck an employee in the upper left arm resulting in a fractured arm and flesh loss.

Two employees were helping welders by holding a 16" flange when a flash fire occurred. The first employee suffered a puncture wound from a vent pipe and burns to the face. The second employee suffered burns to the back of his neck, his back, and his right arm.

An employee was plumbing in a separator on a natural gas line that had pressure in it. The line blew up and knocked the employee to the ground, spraying him with dirt and rocks. He fractured his skull and suffered cuts to his arms.

A employee was anchoring a heavy pipe into a rack when the pipe slipped. The pipe pinched his left hand and middle finger when he went to catch it, resulting in an amputation of the middle finger above the middle knuckle.
An employee was re-dressing a setting tool. The employee's right little finger was caught between the setting sleeve and a mandrel porthole. The tip was amputated.
An employee was transferring product from a tote to a truck when static caused vapors to ignite. The employee was burned on the abdomen and face and has a possible broken ankle.

An employee assisting in hydro-excavation operations sustained injuries to the left foot from a pressure washer being operated by another employee. The injured employee sustained lacerations on the left foot a few inches above the ankle and between the little toe and the fourth toe.
An employee was loading an empty coil tubing reel onto a trailer using a crane. The reel fell off the trailer and struck the employee breaking the tibia and fibula.
After work (installing wellheads and valves in the field), an employee suffered severe heat exhaustion and cramping and was hospitalized.
An employee was setting pipes on the ground and working on pipe support. The ground fell out, causing the pipes to slip and crush the employee's right leg.
An employee fell from the top of a truck and landed on the ground, breaking his leg in two places and requiring surgery.
An employee was operating a gate valve. The handwheel kicked back and struck his arm, breaking the forearm and wrist. The employee was hospitalized, requiring surgery.

An employee was opening a hatch on the top portion of a tanker truck. They tripped and fell approximately 8 feet to the ground, sustaining fractures to multiple ribs and their right wrist, as well as a punctured lung.
An employee fell while walking on a sidewalk. The employee's right shoulder hit a welding machine, causing a fracture to the right upper arm.
An employee was starting a pressure washer when a plug from the block valve blew out and struck the employee in the face, fracturing the left cheek and jaw.

An employee approached the driver of a semi truck with a belly dumper trailer to notify them that they smelled burning brakes. While the employee was checking the front brakes, the brakes released and the truck rolled backward over their leg. The employee sustained a fractured leg, ankle, and toe.

On April 29, 2024, at around 8:45 AM, an employee was making a fuel delivery to a 300-gallon fuel tank that was located on top of pea gravel at a customer's site. The gravel started to shift during the delivery and the employee jumped from their step ladder about 24-30 inches to the gravel to avoid the tank and then fell. The employee sustained a laceration to their left eyebrow and three broken ribs on their left side.

An employee was installing a compressor piston. He tripped and fell backward while the piston was in his lap. As he landed, the little finger of his left hand became caught between the piston and compressor piping resulting in a partial amputation of the fingertip. The employee required stitches and the fingertip was reattached.

An employee was pulling serial numbers off a hydraulic valve. The strap that was being used to hold the valve snapped and the valve fell, pinning the employee against a forklift. The employee suffered broken ribs and was hospitalized.
An employee was pulling an LP gas hose to fill a residential LP tank and slipped on ice and fell breaking his hip.

An employee working on the drilling floor was picking up the jerk chain for the tongs when the driller applied tension to the chain. The employee got the fingers of his left hand pinched between the headache post and the chain.

An employee was troubleshooting an electrical problem at a well site. The employee touched an electrical panel with an impact wrench when an electrical arc occurred, resulting in burns to the employee's right hand and forearm.
An employee was performing winching operations on a flatbed when their left hand was pinched between a winch hook and a nylon bridle resulting in the amputation of his left index finger.
While attaching a lifting sling to a truck, an employee was struck by a backhoe bucket. The employee suffered a right hip injury.
An employee was retrieving a Christmas tree from a shelf using a ladder. He missed a step and fell to the concrete floor. He sustained injury to his head and wrist.

A contractor hired to replace an old pipeline damaged it with a backhoe and created a leak. There was a trench about 3 feet deep and 18 inches wide. The injured employee was on scene to evaluate the leak. He moved from one side of the trench to the other. The soil on the opposite side gave way and exposed a tree root; he hit his chin on that root. The employee broke two bones in his left leg about 2 inches from his ankle.

An employee fell from a rolling ladder while operating a valve, landing on a concrete surface about 4 feet below. The employee suffered a broken left femur and a dislocated right elbow and was hospitalized, undergoing surgery.

On 1/14/2015 at approximately 11:23a.m. an employee was using a blow down system on a National 340 pump to blow out water in the hard line. Once the 4 inch suction hose was drained, the suction hose was disconnected and a cam lock was placed on the suction hose coming from the pump. The four inch butterfly valve for the suction was left open allowing air to pressure up against the cam lock cap. The employee used this system to build air and blow down the fluid in the tubing line to the tank. The employee was standing in front of the manifold and slightly to the right approximately one foot away. When the employee opened up the manifold, the cam lock cap popped free hitting him in the shin.

An employee was moving a piece of an I-beam for welding when it rolled off the cribbing. The employee went to catch it when it fell and crushed the employee's finger, resulting in a partial amputation.

An employee had been unloading tires from the back of a pickup truck. The employee went to step down out of the back of the pickup truck and stepped on the lift gate in a vertical position. The lift gate tipped and employee fell, impacting their side on the upright liftgate. The employee sustained five fractured ribs and a punctured right lung. The employee was hospitalized.

While cleaning equipment prior to rig down, an employee was working with a rig contractor to rig down a centrifuge slide with a forklift. The employee was sitting on a beam under the centrifuge and behind the slide when the slide slipped off the forklift, swinging and pinning the employee against the beam of the centrifuge. He sustained a fractured tibia and fibula just below the left knee.
While climbing off a work platform, an employee lost his grip on the side rail and his leg was caught between the rail and platform. His leg was severed and required hospitalization.

An employee was attempting to reposition the fork on a telehandler. His right pinky finger was between the fork and the mounting bracket when the fork shifted and swung back, crushing his pinky finger.
An employee was shocked while checking a breaker with a meter. The employee sustained a burn to their left middle finger.

An employee was driving a street sweeper down a well pad access road when he applied the brakes, slid into a ditch, hit a mound, went airborne, and rolled two times. He suffered fractured ribs, a collapsed lung, and a fractured pelvis.
Two employees were trying to adjust a 1,500-pound accumulator. It tipped over and caught one of the employees, breaking his right leg.

An employee working in the maintenance garage was conducting an oil change on a vehicle and was looking for a drum to collect the oil. The employee and another employee found a partially full drum that was labeled as methanol. The employees thought the drum potentially contained water. They took the drum outside and poured some of the contents on the ground. The employee that was conducting the oil change applied a lighter to the material on the ground. The material caught on fire. As the other employee was attempting to move the drum out of the area, some of the liquid exited the drum, and was ignited by the fire on the ground. The employee that was conducting the oil change suffered second degree burns to his right leg from the knee to the ankle.

On 2/20/2016, at around 4:00 p.m., an employee was using a machine called a planner to prep the poly pipe for welding repairs when a short burst of flame occurred. The employee received second degree burns to the side of the face and neck and was hospitalized overnight.

An employee was going to heat up a burrito in the dog house (work trailer). When the employee went to turn on the stove/cook top, a flash fire occurred due to gas accumulation. The employee sustained burns to the face and neck, and had second degree burns on both hands.

While checking on equipment on the back of a welding truck, an employee fell off the back of the truck to the ground about 36 inches below. The employee suffered multiple fractures and was hospitalized.

Two employees were loosening a union. One of the employees was striking the union to loosen it when the ball valve broke off the pipe on the pressure side. The ball valve struck the employee's head and knocked him over. His head landed on a piece of piping.
An employee was putting a tire on a vehicle when the jack slipped and struck his left wrist, causing six fractures.
On April 23, 2019, an employee was testing the voltage on a 34.5-kV, 4160/2400 step-down transformer when an arc flash burned the upper right part of his body. He was hospitalized.

An employee was making welding repairs to one of the pad eyes on a 30 inch Blow Out Preventer (BOP). The task required the employee to place the BOP on a table positioner. While welding the 14,000 lbs. piece, it fell from the table crushing the employee's left foot.
An employee was helping to load a truck. A pipe in the truck began shifting and he went to try to grab it when he fell backward to the ground and broke an arm.

An employee was performing backflow operations at a tank battery. After shutting a valve, pressure built in the line causing the line to rupture. The employee was standing near the line when it ruptured and their right arm and the right side of their torso were struck by hot oil, water, and sand (approximately 147 degrees) resulting in severe burns requiring hospitalization.

Employees were rigging down the workover rig at about 11:30 a.m., on July 5, when an employee's right thumb and first finger were caught between the derrick tip section and stop plate. The employee's thumb had to be surgically amputated.

An employee was waiting inside of his vehicle for the pipe to pull through and heard the equipment make an erratic sound. The employee stepped out of his vehicle to check on the pulling equipment. As he approached the cable pulling equipment, the cable released from its guide/pulley and whipped back and forth striking the employee and breaking an arm.

An employee was attaching drill pipe to elevators using his hands. His fingers got stuck between the elevator and the drill pipe, which broke two fingers (pointer and middle finger of the right hand).
An employee was working on the rig floor when they began to experience dizziness and cramping in their legs and arms due to dehydration and heat stress. The employee was hospitalized.
An engine backfired and ignited gas in the building, causing an explosion and fire that burned an employee's face and neck.

An employee was refilling a bottle with a cleaning solution when bleach entered the bottle and it exploded. The employee inhaled the fumes and experienced difficulty breathing and burns to her throat, resulting in hospitalization.

An employee was operating a hand grinder. When the employee stood up to respond to another employee, the cord/plug of the hand grinder struck him in the neck. The employee was hospitalized and received stitches in the neck area.

Two employees were observing a crew who was in the process of reconfiguring a well head. Trapped pressure was released within the well and blew shrapnel (nuts, bolt, plastic parts of the inside of the valves that are part of the well head tree) at the two employees. One employee received an amputation injury to his right thumb. The other employee received shrapnel injuries to his body requiring him to be hospitalized and undergo surgery to remove the shrapnel.

An employee was cleaning oil off the floor of a turbine unit with a pressure washer at a compressor station when he began to feel dizzy and later experienced headaches. He was hospitalized for heat exhaustion.

An employee entered the subfloor to survey the area before submitting a plan for repair. There is a submersible pump and an electrical outlet for the pump to plug into under the subfloor. The employee touched an electrical source and sustained an electrical shock. The employee sustained a burn injury, internal damage, and was rendered unconscious. The employee was hospitalized.

A crew was removing bolts from the pump's spool piece and rigging the hoist to hold the elevated spool piece out. The crew replaced the witch's hat inside the pump and began to reinstall the spool piece when a burst of fire came out of the pipe and struck the injured employee's face and hand resulting in burns.
An employee slipped while working on a blowout preventer, falling about 2 feet to the ground and suffering a broken thumb.

While working on a saltwater disposal system, an employee was checking the rotation of a pump and noticed the oil tank was bulging at the bottom. The employee ran to get away from it when a flash fire erupted. The employee sustained second degree burns to the face, lower back, and both hands.
An employee was walking down stairs when she tripped and fell, injuring her left leg and ankle.
An employee was walking on the company road to work when he was struck by another employee who was driving a car away from the premises. He suffered a spinal injury and head laceration.

An employee was helping to move a piece of casing off a guide wire from a rig. The casing was on a pipe rack. As the pipe was pushed to move it out of the guide wire, the pipe rolled and caught his right hand, pinching his middle finger and resulting in partial amputation of the fingertip.
At 2:17 p.m. on March 29, 2021, an employee fell while stepping out of a tractor. He landed on the ground and suffered a broken left hip.

At 9:00 AM, on 5/10/16, an employee and a coworker were preparing to replace a malfunctioning gauge board on an asphalt tank. They transferred contents from the malfunctioning tank to another tank and shut down the malfunctioning tank. Every energy source was off/locked out. Using an impact wrench, the employee began loosening/removing the bolts holding the manway cover on the tank. After he loosened several bolts, some hot liquid asphalt splashed out from behind the cover onto the concrete pad and onto his hands, arms, and legs. He suffered second and third degree burns to both arms, hands, and legs, requiring hospitalization and surgery.
While performing well servicing operations, an employee became lightheaded and began vomiting. He was hospitalized for dehydration.
An employee slipped and fell on icy ground while unloading a down hole pump off of a trailer. The employee sustained a fractured hip.
An employee was working in an oilfield cleaning a sand hopper. He got caught in a hydraulic gate fracturing both femurs.
Employees were putting rebar together with chicken wire at a construction site when one employee became ill and dizzy, requiring hospitalization for heat exhaustion.

An employee was dismounting from the bumper of a pickup truck. As the employee was stepping off, the bumper components slipped out from under him, causing him to fall to the ground. The employee sustained a closed fracture of his left ankle, requiring surgery.

Employees were installing a manual start switch on a 480-volt variable speed drive motor controller on a saltwater disposal (SWD) well control panel when an arc flash occurred. Two employee sustained burns and were hospitalized.
An employee was lowering elevators while trying to couple a joint of tubing coming from a well. The employee's right hand was caught in a pinch point resulting in amputation of the ring fingertip.
An employee was on top of a coil, trying to align its head end with its tail end for stationary welding. The coil clamp was lowered onto the employee's left foot, amputating the big toe.

An employee was setting up a board over a 3-foot deep excavation so that he could access the control valve to stop a leak. The employee fell into the excavation that was filled with hot water and suffered burns to the feet, leg and knee.

An employee was pumping chemicals in a hot oiler pump truck. A chemical reaction caused an explosion that propelled the employee into the back of another vehicle. The employee suffered facial contusions.
An employee was draining condensate out of the treater line when a flash fire occurred, causing second degree burns.
An employee sustained a partial left index finger amputation when high winds caused the compressor building door to slam on the employee's finger.

Two employees were working on a forklift due to a belt issue. The injured employee was working on the belt when the other employee started the forklift. The belt and pulley in the forklift motor then amputated the injured employee's right index fingertip.

An employee was bleeding down injection lines, using a 36-inch pipe wrench, to let hydrates thaw overnight. A valve was opened and pressure (about 900 psi) was released, causing a section of pipe to come loose and strike the employee's leg above the knee. He was hospitalized.

An employee was removing a "Christmas tree" fitting from a pressurized wax tank. The pressure in the wax tank caused the wax to burst from the fitting and onto the employee. The employee was hospitalized for burns to the body.

On January 11, 2018, at approximately 11:00 a.m., an employee was attempting to drive an ATV up a steep incline when it tipped over backwards. He was hospitalized with a fractured lower vertebra and internal bleeding.
An employee experienced heat stress.

An employee was lowering a scaffold board using a rope and pulley assembly when the board slipped out of the rope and fell. The board caught a tangle in the rope and caused the hook end of the rope to shoot upward, where it hit the employee in the face and head. The employee suffered a probable fracture or concussion and tissue damage in the right eye area.
An employee was exiting a truck when he lost his footing while descending the cab stairs. He fell to the ground and injured his left elbow, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was dispatched to an oil and gas weld site to pick up produced water. When he made it to the worksite, he set his truck in position, connected the hose, and engaged the vacuum pump. A fire then occurred, causing second and third degree burns to both of his arms and part of his torso, as well as minor burns to his neck, face, and ear.

On July 17, 2015, at approximately 1:45pm, an employee was hospitalized after suffering two broken bones to his lower left leg. Before the incident, the employee was standing on the third rung of a 12-foot stepladder, tightening bolts on a flange with a torque wrench. While applying pressure to the wrench, a reducer on the wrench broke, causing the employee to lose his balance. As he stepped down 34" to the gravel surface, he landed awkwardly on his left foot, causing fractures.
An employee was hospitalized from heat exhaustion.

Employees were pulling up piping on a workover rig. The anchor on the piping got caught on the slip, then the slip got caught on the work floor, pulling it up while the employee was standing on it. When the work floor broke away from the slip, the flooring fell back down to the ground. This caused the employee to fall and sustain a right leg fracture that required hospitalization.

An employee was using a portable grinder with a wire brush wheel to clean a metallic natural gas pipe in preparation for welding. The flow of natural gas had been stopped with a metallic stopper pin. As the employee was using the grinder, the stopper pin became dislodged from a seated position, resulting in a brief ignition of the natural gas. The employee suffered first and second degree burns to the right side of his face and nose.
An employee was opening a gate when the last finger of the employee's left hand was pinched in a roller; the fingertip was amputated.

Two employees were performing routine maintenance activities on instrumentation equipment when a caustic line going into an instrument began to release sodium hydroxide and propane, resulting in burns to the face and upper body due to contact with sodium hydroxide. Both employees were hospitalized.
An employee was repairing a pack installation under tension. Upon pushing the pack, the employee sustained a left calf strain and was hospitalized.

An employee was tracing an acetonitrile solution pipeline to verify which pipe was leaking from the pipe rack when he came into contact with the chemical mist. He experienced a headache and signs of exposure to acetonitrile, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was loading a truck with caustic potash. A valve gasket failed and sprayed the employee with the caustic potash, resulting in burns to their face, back, chest, and head.

An employee was acting as a spotter for a forklift operator. While its forks were being raised, the forklift came into contact with a power line. The employee was touching the forklift's metal frame at the time and was shocked on the left palm. The employee suffered burns to both the left palm and the sole of the left foot.

An employee was heating an asphalt product with a propane torch to close a lid on a tank when a flash fire occurred. The employee suffered second degree burns to the hand and first degree burns to the face.

While working in the Rigger Shop, an employee was using channel lock pliers to disconnect two pieces of pipe that were bolted together. The pipe was raised by a crane.
